His experiments with long receiving wires produced the highly directional wave antenna that still carries his surname. IEEE records document a career spanning early radio, global communications, engineering leadership, and more than forty patents.

A North Haven-born pioneer of long-distance radio reception, Harold Beverage graduated from the University of Maine in 1915 and began his career at General Electric. At RCA he led transoceanic receiver development, rose to vice president of research and development, and applied his communications expertise to wartime work including radio links supporting D-Day. IEEE’s institutional biography records an unusually vivid early-radio episode: as a teenager on North Haven, Harold Beverage built a homemade wireless station and received signals from Carpathia after it rescued Titanic survivors, years before his professional work on long-distance radio and the Beverage antenna.

rows: James Beveridge Sr. was born around 1700, likely in Scotland (family tradition places his birth in Dunfermline, Fife). He later migrated to Marblehead, Massachusetts and became the patriarch of the Beverage family.
Marriage of James Beveridge Sr. and Sarah Bennett
James Beveridge Sr. married Sarah Bennett at St. Michael's Church in Marblehead, Massachusetts. This was his first marriage.
Marriage of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White
After the death of his first wife Sarah Bennett, James Beveridge Sr. married Mary White in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Marriage of James Beveridge Sr. and Sarah Holman
James Beveridge Sr. married his third wife, Sarah Holman, in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
James Beveridge Jr. was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts. He later settled on the Fox Islands (North Haven) and married Jean McKinney White.
Sarah Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Sarah Bennett, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts. She later married Peter Ayers.
Susannah Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Jane Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Mary Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Marriage of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White
James Beveridge Jr. married Jean (Jane) McKinney White, widow of Nicholas White, in Georgetown, Maine. This union linked the Beveridge and White families.

Capt. Thomas Beverage (born Thomas Beveridge) was born at Mere’s Point, Topsham, Maine, in a stockaded house built by Capt. John Minot. He would later become a privateer and town clerk of North Haven.
Mercy Beveridge Henry, daughter of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White, was born. She later married Henry Henry.
Mercy Kent was born in Marshfield, Massachusetts. She married Capt. Thomas Beverage and settled on North Haven Island.
Sarah Beveridge Kent, daughter of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White, was born. She later married Benjamin Kent, creating a double in-law tie between the Beveridge and Kent families.

Family letters and deeds indicate that Capt. Thomas Beverage participated in the Boston Tea Party on 16 December 1773. He traveled from the Fox Islands to Marblehead and joined the group of patriots who destroyed tea in Boston Harbor.
Thomas sells 120 acres on North Fox Island

On 3 January 1774, Thomas Beveridge of Marblehead sold a 120-acre tract on North Fox Island to William Blackler for 53 pounds 13 shillings. The land bounded on William Perry’s land, a pond, Ezekiel Kent’s land and the thoroughfare.
Marriage of Thomas Beverage and Mercy Kent
Thomas Beverage married Mercy Kent at Trinity Church in Boston, Massachusetts. Mercy was the daughter of Ezekiel Kent and Susanna Bryant Winslow.
William Blackler reconveys land to Thomas
On 1 March 1779, William Blackler reconveyed the 120-acre tract on North Fox Island back to Thomas Beverage for £200. The land now measured 125 acres.
John White Beverage, eldest son of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He was named after Mercy’s son by her first husband John White.
Nathaniel Winslow Beverage, second son of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later became a deacon in Camden.
Benjamin Kent Beverage, third son of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He was named after his uncle Benjamin Kent.
Thomas Beverage testifies about Robert Duglase

In 1781, Thomas Beverage testified that Robert Duglase of Fox Island procured a pass from Capt. Henry Mowitt for fishing and bought a schooner from Billings Putnam of Newburyport. This testimony was recorded on 1 June 1786.
Fox Islands petition for land titles

In March 1785, the inhabitants of the Fox Islands Plantation met at the home of Benjamin Kent and Sarah Beveridge Kent to petition the Massachusetts General Court for clear title to lands occupied before 1 June 1784. James Beveridge Sr. was chosen moderator and Thomas Beverage was elected Plantation Clerk.
Mercy Kent Beverage, fourth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island.
Sarah ("Sally") Beverage, fifth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She later married Benjamin Kent.
Lydia Winslow Beverage, sixth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She died young in 1792.
James Beverage, seventh child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later became a tanner and landowner.
Josiah Winslow Beverage, eighth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later served as town selectman and co-owned the family mill.
Lydia Winslow Beverage, ninth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She died in 1829.
Abigail Beverage, tenth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She died the following day.
Abigail Beverage, infant daughter of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, died the day after her birth on North Haven Island.
Thomas purchases 100 acres from Nathaniel Crockett Jr.
Thomas Beverage purchased 100 acres on North Haven from Nathaniel Crockett Jr. This land later formed part of the family estate. The deed was registered in 1806.
Thomas sells 120 acres to Samuel Thomas
On 3 November 1784, Thomas Beverage sold 120 acres of land on North Fox Island to Samuel Thomas for 150 pounds. The land later came into Kent and Beverage hands.

On 9 March 1781, Thomas Beverage and Abigail Dyer witnessed David Woster Sr. transferring half of his North Haven land to his infant son David Woster Jr. for $500. The transaction was recorded in 1801.
On 21 May 1788, Thomas Beverage settled accounts with Abel Whitman, receiving payment in full for half of the island he had sold him.
Thomas Beverage registers his cattle mark
On 9 March 1789, Thomas Beverage registered his cattle mark in the town records: the left ear split and a half-penny out of the foreside of the right ear.
1790 Census enumeration of the Beverage household

The 1790 U.S. Census recorded the household of Thomas Beverage on North Haven with two males over 16 (Thomas and John), four males under 16 (Nathaniel, Benjamin, James, Josiah) and five females (Mercy, Mercy Jr., Sarah, Lydia and an unknown female).

On 10 October 1791, Thomas Beverage and William Cooper witnessed James and Elizabeth Heard selling Pulpit Harbor land for 90 pounds. The land was near Samuel Lewis’s property.
On 27 March 1792, Thomas Beverage and Levi Smith witnessed Charles Stewart and Abel Whitman selling Eames Island (40 acres) to John Brooks for 30 pounds.
On 6 April 1795, Thomas Beverage and his son Nathaniel Beverage witnessed Charles Stewart selling 38¾ acres to John Newbury.
On 20 May 1796, Thomas Beverage and Cornelius Bramhall witnessed Levi Smith selling 50 acres to Thomas Cooper for $250.
Thomas sells land to William Vinal
On 18 April 1797, Thomas Beverage sold a parcel of land near the North Harbor to William Vinal of Vinalhaven for $4. The deed was witnessed by Gabriel Johonnot and George Ulmer.
Witness to George White land sale
On 16 September 1800, Thomas Beverage and his son John White Beverage witnessed George White selling land by the Pond Swamp to Joseph Maddocks for $100.
Sale of mill shares to Henry Alexander
On 28 February 1806, Thomas Beverage sold Henry Alexander 1/8 share of the sawmill and 1/4 share of the grist mill for $300. The deed was witnessed by William Vinall and William Norwood.
Repurchase of land and mills from Henry Alexander
On 15 December 1807, Henry Alexander sold back to Thomas Beverage 115 acres, a dwelling house, barn, and shares in a sawmill and grist mill for $1500.
Robert Henry sells 100 acres to Oliver Amsbury

On 17 February 1808, Robert Henry of Topsham sold 100 acres on North Haven to Oliver Amsbury of Vinalhaven for $350, reserving 60 acres previously conveyed to David Perry. The deed was witnessed by Thomas Beverage and David Wooster Jr.
Thomas sells 115 acres to Josiah and James
On 11 May 1811, Thomas Beverage sold 115 acres, a dwelling house, barn, and shares in a sawmill and grist mill to his sons Josiah Winslow Beverage and James Beverage for $2,500.
Sale of 12 acres to Cornelius Bramhall
On 17 April 1813, Thomas Beverage sold 12 acres on the northeast cove of North Harbor to Cornelius Bramhall for $150. The deed was witnessed by Sarah and Sally Bramhall.
Sale of land to Malatiah Luce and Jonathan Smith
On 23 January 1814, Thomas Beverage sold land at the head of the Mill Pond to Malatiah Luce and Jonathan Smith for $150. The deed was witnessed by John Wagg and Nathaniel Beverage.
Thomas Beverage appointed delegate to Brunswick convention
In September 1816, Thomas Beverage was selected by the town to serve as delegate to the convention at Brunswick to discuss the separation of Maine from Massachusetts.
Mercy Kent Beverage, wife of Capt. Thomas Beverage, died on North Haven Island.
Marriage of James Beverage and Jemima Crabtree
James Beverage married Jemima Crabtree on North Haven Island. Their union connected the Beverage family with the Crabtrees, another prominent island family.
Benjamin Crabtree Beverage, eldest son of James Beverage and Jemima Crabtree, was born on North Haven Island.
Harrison Beverage, second son of James and Jemima Beverage, was born on North Haven Island.
Albert Glover Beverage, third son of James and Jemima Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later became a deacon and farmer.
Lucy C. Beverage, only daughter of James and Jemima Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She later died in 1850 after exposure to mercury in her father’s tannery.

A targeted 2026 search of historical newspapers, Vinalhaven/North Haven histories, and mercury/mercurial/quicksilver/tannery variants did not locate independent contemporaneous corroboration. Treat the cause as unverified unless a stronger record is found.

Jemima Crabtree Beverage died on North Haven Island, likely from a hemorrhage linked to mercurial poisoning from the tannery.

After his divorce from Sarah W. Loveland, Benjamin Crabtree Beverage married his second cousin Amelia Beverage on North Haven Island.
James Beverage died on North Haven Island. His death, and that of his daughter Lucy two days later, were attributed to mercury poisoning from his tannery.

Benjamin Kent Beverage died on North Haven Island at age 72.
Benjamin Crabtree Beverage died during a diphtheria epidemic on North Haven Island. He was a deacon and farmer.
Marriage of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Margaret Leadbetter
Samuel Carver Beverage married Ruth Margaret Leadbetter in a double wedding on North Haven. Ruth’s brother Isaac Leadbetter married Jennie Sawyer at the same ceremony.
Hiram Stone Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island. He later operated the family farm at Sunnyside.
Albert Lewis Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Marston Leadbetter Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Olive Mary Beverage, daughter of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Nettie Ellen Beverage, daughter of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Elroy Victor Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
George Dewey Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Edith Etta Beverage, daughter of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Wilson Freemont Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Alma Marie Beverage, daughter of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island. She died in infancy.
Birth of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage
Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage was born in Dorchester, Massachusetts. He later became a minister and father of Albion Pierson Beverage III.
Marriage of Orris Lyford Beverage and Rose Emma Pierson
Orris Lyford Beverage married Rose Emma Pierson at Tenants Harbor, Maine. Their marriage produced eight children.
Marriage of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Elizabeth Reed
Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage married Grace Elizabeth Reed in Dorchester, Massachusetts. They later raised their family in Dresden, Maine.
Nancy Beverage, daughter of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Reed, was born. She later lived in Maine.
Grace Pauline Beverage, daughter of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Reed, was born.
Birth of Albion Pierson Beverage III
Albion Pierson Beverage III, son of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Elizabeth Reed, was born (approximate date). He later maintained the family cottage on North Haven.
Janice Lynn Marshall (later Beverage) was born around 1940. She married Albion Pierson Beverage III around 1962 and was the family genealogist.
Marriage of Hiram Stone Beverage and Ruby Hazel Taylor
Hiram Stone Beverage married Ruby Hazel Taylor around 1916 on North Haven Island. They had one son, Samuel Hiram Beverage.
Samuel Hiram Beverage, only child of Hiram Stone Beverage and Ruby Hazel Taylor, was born at Sunnyside farm on North Haven Island.
Marriage of Samuel Hiram Beverage and Eleanor Mae Sargent
Samuel Hiram Beverage married Eleanor Mae Sargent in Somerville, Massachusetts in 1945. They raised five children and were instrumental in preserving North Haven history.
Death of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage
Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage died in Silver Spring, Maryland at age 43. He was buried in Fuller Cemetery on North Haven Island.
Death of Ruth Margaret Leadbetter Beverage
Ruth Margaret Leadbetter Beverage died on North Haven Island at age 92, having raised twelve children.
Death of Ruby Hazel Taylor Beverage
Ruby Hazel Taylor Beverage, wife of Hiram Stone Beverage and mother of Samuel Hiram Beverage, died on North Haven Island.
Robert Elliot Beverage, son of Albion Pierson Beverage III and Janice Marshall, was born (approximate date). He later married Heather Beverage and co-owns property on North Haven.
Marriage of Albion Pierson Beverage III and Janice Marshall
Albion Pierson Beverage III married Janice Lynn Marshall around 1962. They celebrated over 60 years of marriage and preserved the family cottage on North Haven.
Marriage of Robert Elliot Beverage and Heather Ellen Beverage
Robert Elliot Beverage married Heather Ellen Beverage (approximate date). They have three children: Lauren, Sarah and Daniel.
Purchase of 128 S Orchard Street, Wallingford
Robert Elliot Beverage and Heather Beverage purchased a home at 128 S Orchard Street in Wallingford, Connecticut, where they raised their family.
Founding of North Haven Historical Society
After returning permanently to North Haven in 1973, Samuel Hiram Beverage and his wife Eleanor helped found the North Haven Historical Society to preserve island history.
In 1974, Arthur Walter Beverage Sr., a great-great-grandson of Capt. Thomas Beverage, sold Old Barn Hill to Henry Meigs. The hill was later developed as a private residence.
Death of Grace Elizabeth Reed Beverage
Grace Elizabeth Reed Beverage, widow of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage, died in Dresden, Maine at age 99.
Samuel Hiram Beverage died on North Haven Island at age 97. He was a radio enthusiast, WWII veteran, and co-founder of the North Haven Historical Society.
Death of Janice Lynn Marshall Beverage
Janice Lynn Marshall Beverage died in Ocala, Florida after a long life dedicated to her family and genealogy research.

The 2024 North Haven tax commitment list recorded Albion Pierson Beverage III and Robert E. Beverage as co-owners of parcel 13-004-D at 216 Beverage Colony Road, continuing the family’s land ownership on the island.
Harrison Beverage chosen as a representative

Vinalhaven's published town history records that Harrison Beverage of North Haven was chosen as a representative in 1859 and later resigned; Lewis Leadbetter was elected in his place at a December special meeting.
Documented in a published 1889 town history
Albert G. Beverage listed as a representative
The representative list in Vinalhaven's published town history names Albert G. Beverage of North Haven for 1878.
Documented in a published 1889 town history
A Maine state year-book entry for North Haven lists Fremont Beverage as school superintendent and gives February 25, 1915 as the date associated with his service as a justice.
Historical directory transcription; appointment record remains a useful follow-up
Harold Beverage graduates from the University of Maine
Harold H. Beverage completed his electrical-engineering degree at the University of Maine in 1915 before beginning his engineering career with General Electric.
Corroborated by IEEE biography and oral history
Harold Beverage receives radio receiving-system patent
U.S. Patent 1,381,089 was issued to Harold H. Beverage for a directional radio receiving system after an application filed on April 10, 1920. The patent was assigned to General Electric Company.
Harold Beverage receives the Liebmann Memorial Prize
The Institute of Radio Engineers recognized Harold Beverage with its Morris N. Liebmann Memorial Prize for his contributions to transoceanic radio and directional antennas.
Hiram Beverage builds the Mill Stream dam

Two independent local-history accounts identify Hiram “Hightie” Beverage as the builder of the present Mill Stream dam in 1932. The resulting brackish pond became known locally as Hightie's Pond and later supported oyster aquaculture.
Corroborated by two independent local-history accounts; town or engineering record still sought
Harold Beverage serves as IRE president
Harold H. Beverage served as president of the Institute of Radio Engineers in 1937.
Harold Beverage receives the IRE Medal of Honor
The Institute of Radio Engineers awarded Harold H. Beverage its Medal of Honor in recognition of his radio research, inventions, practical engineering work, and service to the institute.
Harold Beverage retires from RCA leadership
Harold Beverage retired in 1958 from his RCA Communications research-and-development leadership and radio-research directorship, then continued working as a communications consultant.
Samuel H. Beverage receives North Haven's Boston Post Cane
North Haven awarded its Boston Post Cane to Samuel H. Beverage on December 4, 2010, two days before his ninety-third birthday, recognizing him as the town's oldest resident.
Contemporary community register corroborated by obituary
Benjamin Beverage represents Vinalhaven at Maine’s Constitutional Convention
Benjamin Beverage was Vinalhaven’s delegate to the 1819 convention that framed the constitution for the new State of Maine as separation from Massachusetts approached.
Benjamin Beverage serves in the Maine House
The State of Maine’s 1823 civil-government record lists Benjamin Beverage as representative for Vinalhaven together with a long group of neighboring islands.
Verified by official Maine legislative record
Benjamin Beverage writes a history of Vinalhaven

A surviving ink manuscript by Benjamin Beverage, dated December 20, 1819 and now in the Maine Historical Society’s William D. Williamson papers, recounts Vinalhaven’s settlement, land distribution, vessels and religion. It provides a rare first-hand historical voice from a member of the family.
Frank Beverage joins North Haven petition to Congress

The Congressional Record lists Frank Beverage and other North Haven residents among petitioners asking Congress to pass the Kenyon-Sheppard interstate liquor bill, showing direct participation in a nationally contested Progressive Era policy issue.
Frank Beverage serves as auctioneer for Pulpit Harbor property sale

A Courier-Gazette advertisement announced the public sale of the Sands H. Witherspoon homestead at Pulpit Harbor and named Frank Beverage as auctioneer, documenting another aspect of his local business and community role.
Frank Beverage calls North Haven water-loan bonds as town treasurer

A contemporary Courier-Gazette notice signed by Frank Beverage as North Haven treasurer called a numbered group of municipal water-loan bonds for payment effective September 1, 1926. The notice documents his responsibility for the town’s public finance and water infrastructure debt.
Verified by contemporary public financial notice
Gerald G. Beverage enters U.S. Navy service in World War II

Gerald Beverage entered the U.S. Navy in December 1942 after completing Yale Law School. His obituary reports Pacific Theater service connected with campaigns at Kwajalein, Saipan, Guam, the Philippines and Iwo Jima, and says he left active service in late 1945 as a lieutenant. The timeline deliberately omits an obituary ship-name detail that has not yet been independently verified.
Strongly supported by detailed obituary; specific vessel identity withheld pending independent verification
Teenage Harold Beverage receives Carpathia wireless signals after Titanic disaster

IEEE’s institutional biography reports that Harold Beverage, already experimenting with a homemade wireless station as a teenager, picked up signals from Carpathia, the ship that rescued survivors of the Titanic disaster. The episode foreshadowed the long-distance radio work that later made his name internationally known.
Strongly supported by IEEE institutional biography
James Beverage elected at Topsham’s first town meeting

At Topsham’s first town meeting after incorporation, James Beverage was elected hog constable. The office was modest, but the record places the Beveridge/Beverage family inside the first formal municipal government of the town where the family lived before the Fox Islands generation.
Strongly supported by published transcription of municipal history
John Beverage joins protest over moving Hancock County courts

The Massachusetts House journal recorded a memorial from John Beverage and other inhabitants of Vinalhaven remonstrating against removal of the Hancock County courts from Castine to Buckstown. The petition shows island residents engaging directly with state government over access to county institutions.
Verified by official Massachusetts House journal
John Miller Beverage begins missionary service in Guatemala

After completing Dallas Theological Seminary in 1953, John Miller Beverage was appointed by Central American Mission and served as a missionary in Guatemala until 1972 before returning to work at Dallas Theological Seminary.
John Beverage succeeds Thomas as Vinalhaven town clerk
John Beverage appears as Vinalhaven town clerk in every annual roster from 1799 through 1812, a fourteen-year span immediately following Thomas Beverage’s nine-year tenure.
Strongly supported by near-contemporary town-history roster
Nathaniel Beverage represents Vinalhaven in the Maine House
The official 1828 Maine House payroll lists Nathaniel Beverage as the representative from Vinalhaven, extending the family’s documented participation from island offices into state government.
Verified by official Maine House payroll
Maine authorizes a Pulpit Harbor toll bridge to Beverage family land

A Maine act established the North Haven Bridge Company and authorized a toll bridge over the head of Pulpit Harbor from Enos Cooper’s land to land belonging to James and Josiah Beverage. The law required a bridge at least twelve feet wide and a draw to allow vessels to pass. The act proves the property relationship and proposed infrastructure; it does not by itself prove that the bridge was ultimately built.
Verified authorization in official Maine law; completion not asserted
Norwood Pierson Beveridge Jr. dies during the COVID-19 pandemic

Norwood P. Beveridge Jr., a Harvard-trained attorney and longtime law professor, died on October 31, 2020. His published obituary explicitly identifies COVID-19 as the cause of death, making his death a documented family connection to the global pandemic.
Orris Lyford Beverage graduates from Colby while leading a high school

Colby University’s 1887 catalogue places Orris Lyford Beverage in the graduating class and identifies him as principal of the high school at Hallowell, documenting the start of the education career later associated with him.
Strongly supported by contemporary university catalogue
Samuel Beverage returns to North Haven and helps establish its historical society

After retiring back to North Haven in 1973, Samuel Hiram Beverage worked with Lewis and Ida Haskell in efforts that his obituary credits as instrumental in establishing the North Haven Historical Society, linking his later life directly to preservation of island history.
Samuel Hiram Beverage departs for overseas Signal Corps service

Samuel Beverage’s detailed obituary reports that he sailed from New York on July 16, 1942 and subsequently served as a Master Sergeant and Radio/Communications Chief with the 1060th Signal Company, 323rd Air Service Group across Libya, Tunisia, Egypt, Lebanon, Palestine and Italy through May 1945.
Strongly supported by detailed obituary; original service file remains a desired primary source
Thomas Beverage begins nine-year run as Vinalhaven town clerk

Vinalhaven’s centennial office roster lists Thomas Beverage as town clerk every year from 1790 through 1798. He also appears among the selectmen in 1797, documenting sustained involvement in the island town’s early civil government.
Strongly supported by near-contemporary town-history roster

inventories.name: Unverified Leads
rows: A published sworn statement places Thomas Beverage at Fox Island on June 1, 1786, testifying about a fishing pass he saw in 1781.
Documentary History of the State of Maine Volume XXI; pp. 221–222; PDF 241–242; https://sites.rootsweb.com/~mealhn/books/mehist_v21.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
The statement is directly documented; attribution to the repository captain is probable from name, island and chronology. It does not establish Tea Party participation or military service.
Scan of published edition visually inspected
The Essex Antiquarian reports a February 7, 1733/4 marriage, and Susannah, Mary and Jane living unmarried in Marblehead in 1789 after their mother Sarah’s death.
The Essex Antiquarian volume IX 1905; vol. IX (1905), p. 91 Notes; https://archive.org/details/essexantiquarian09perluoft; accessed 2026-10-14
Published notes cite town records and deeds without a deed locator. Original marriage and 1789 conveyance must be read before adopting the family reconstruction.
Wheeler’s town history names James Beverage and William Alexander as hog constables elected at Topsham’s first town meeting, May 9, 1764.
History of Brunswick Topsham and Harpswell Maine 1878; p. 183; citing Topsham town records; https://archive.org/details/historyofbrunswi01whee; accessed 2026-10-14
The office and name are in the published account; identifying which James requires original town and land records.
Published scan p. 183 viewed; p. 869 text inspected
James and Samuel Beveridge Topsham lots
The early land-owner list places James Beveridge at lot 7 in 1758 and Samuel Beveridge at lot 3 in 1752.
History of Brunswick Topsham and Harpswell Maine 1878; Appendix I p. 869; https://archive.org/details/historyofbrunswi01whee; accessed 2026-10-14
A compiled list is not a deed. Do not infer a sibling relationship or choose between the two James profiles.
Published scan p. 183 viewed; p. 869 text inspected
The genealogy gives Diana parents Benjamin Daggett and Elizabeth Hathaway, husband Nathaniel Beverage, and one son and three daughters.
A History of the Doggett Daggett Family 1894; p. 113 entries 809 and 1033; https://archive.org/details/historyofdoggett00indogg; accessed 2026-10-14
Matching husband and date support identity, but this is a compiled genealogy. Its parents’ 1766 intention and church records are still unverified.
Benjamin Kent junior and John Kent
Edited Woodruff biographies identify Benjamin Kent (1798–1882) and John Kent (1786–1874) as sons of Benjamin and Sarah Beverage, with spouses Deborah Thomas and Nancy Luce respectively.

Benjamin Kent biographical subject; Subject biographies and footnotes; https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/benjamin-kent; accessed 2026-10-14
John Kent biographical subject; Subject biographies and footnotes; https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/john-kent; accessed 2026-10-14
Potential collateral relatives. Do not attach to Sarah born 1785, who could not be John’s mother. Verify town records and the 1793 father’s deed.
Edited text and footnotes directly viewed; Edited text and footnotes directly viewed
Seaview transcription gives Frank’s death as May 16, 1958 and identifies wife May U. Calderwood.
Seaview Cemetery; p. 2 Frank entry; p. 3 May entry; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/seaview_cemetery.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
Exact January 14, 1861 birth matches baseline, but stone photograph or death certificate has not been obtained.
Transcription read; selected pages visually inspected; original stones not inspected
p. 2 Frank entry; p. 3 May entry
NHHS describes a house on Old Barn Hill built in 1819 and a farm inherited by Frank in 1880.
Pulpit Harbor The Old Village; p. 7; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
Institutional narrative provides no deed or probate locator. Inheritance source and precise parcel identity require proof; no complete title chain exists here.
Directly viewed text and selected PDF pages
Elmira Carver Beverage and Isa Beverage
NHHS identifies Elmira as Isa’s mother and associates them with the store at the end of Beach Bridge.

Pulpit Harbor The Old Village; Village p. 14; Fuller pp. 1–2; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
Fuller Cemetery; Village p. 14; Fuller pp. 1–2; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/fuller_cemetery.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
Institutional account and cemetery family entries agree; deeds and business directory entries remain necessary.
Directly viewed text and selected PDF pages; Transcription read; selected pages visually inspected; original stones not inspected
NHHS describes Alvin and Marion Beverage’s Blue Point farm passing to Nortons then Chestons, and John H. and Cora Beverage’s farm becoming the Lamont estate Sky Farm.
Pulpit Harbor The Old Village; p. 7; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
Historical narrative only; transfer dates, legal descriptions and grantees are not proved. No current ownership is asserted.
Directly viewed text and selected PDF pages
NHHS names Elsie, Jennie and Linda Beverage among the first 1907 high school graduates and Nettie Beverage Crockett as class of 1912.
A Free High School; Graduation paragraphs; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/a-free-high-school.html; accessed 2026-10-14
Documented institutional names; similarly named family members must be identified through school registers before profile attachment.
A Calderwood entry records Lowell Beverage playing piano at church on August 9, 1925.
Tonny and Annie Calderwood diaries 1925; p. 12 August 9; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1925.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
First name, island and musical career fit; middle name absent. Do not attribute to another Lowell or assume a formal appointment.
Transcription directly searched; selected pages viewed; manuscript not viewed
The diocesan memorial reports a roughly 2,000-page manuscript titled Universal Harmony held at the seminary.
1991 Journal of the Diocese of Virginia Lowell Beveridge memorial; p. 73; PDF p. 38; https://episcopalvirginia.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1991-Diocese_Journal_searchable.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14

Historical location reported in 1991; present custody, extent and access have not been confirmed. Baseline obituary may already mention this; useful retrieval specification, not claimed wholly new biography.
Lowell’s diocesan memorial identifies a surviving brother Lyford Beveridge of Rockland; that brother is absent from the repository’s Orris children list.

1991 Journal of the Diocese of Virginia Lowell Beveridge memorial; p. 73; Orris child list; https://episcopalvirginia.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1991-Diocese_Journal_searchable.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14

Do not create a parent-child link from a single obituary-derived statement. May duplicate the existing Washington Post source; independent birth or census evidence is needed.
Published page scan visually inspected; Repository data directly read
Alton T and Edward M Beverage military inscriptions
Fuller transcription lists Alton T. Beverage, March 23, 1917–November 20, 1965, with Tec4 734 WWII, and Edward M., December 15, 1915–March 5, 1960, with PFC 346 Ord Med Maint Co WWII.
No service file inspected, units not expanded beyond transcription, and parentage not established. These are separate candidates, not merged with similarly named relatives.
Transcription read; selected pages visually inspected; original stones not inspected
Seaview gives Amelia’s death as February 16, 1908 aged 75 years 12 days; its birth column incorrectly repeats 1908.
Proposed death date only. Age-derived birth would conflict with stored January 31; inspect original, do not calculate a replacement birth from this transcription.
Transcription read; selected pages visually inspected; original stones not inspected
Nora Julia Nettie and infant deaths
Seaview supplies Nora C. November 5, 1875; Julia W. January 25, 1876; Nettie M. February 5, 1876; and an infant son March 21, 1872, associated with Albert and Olive.
These refine year-only baseline entries but are transcription leads pending death registers; exact cause of death not established by stones.
Transcription read; selected pages visually inspected; original stones not inspected
Albert and Thomas family Bible records
A secondary Bible directory points to DAR Maine series 2 volume 3 pages 316–317, series 2 volume 17 page 1, and NEHGS manuscript C403.
Beverage Family Bibles index; Beverage Carter and Beverage Kent entries; https://yanceyfamilygenealogy.org/Family_Bibles_starting_with_letter/B/BEVERAGE.htm; accessed 2026-10-14
Only finding aid viewed; Bible contents unknown. Directory says Olive Carter while baseline says Carver, requiring original-page examination.
Index directly viewed; Bible pages not viewed
Beverage Carter and Beverage Kent entries
A Digital Maine search points to James and Lucy Beverage death notices in the Lime Rock Gazette of December 26, 1850.
Lime Rock Gazette December 26 1850; Issue December 26, page unverified; https://digitalmaine.com/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1221&context=lime_rock_gazette; accessed 2026-10-14
Underlying issue blocked. No date, quotation or poisoning conclusion is promoted from the snippet.
NPS research notes point to Olmsted job 06653 for Thomas W. Lamont at North Haven, 1918–1921, and a Carr Point newspaper reference of May 16, 1938.

Olmsted GIS research notes April 2016; Job 06653; Lewiston Evening Journal May 16, 1938 p. 4; https://www.nps.gov/frla/learn/photosmultimedia/upload/Research-notes-for-Olmsted-GIS-April2016.pdf; accessed 2026-10-14
Government hosting does not validate the embedded user-tree claim about Benjamin Kent Beverage. Retrieve original plans, deeds and newspaper.
Downloaded full text searched; cited original job file not inspected
Job 06653; Lewiston Evening Journal May 16, 1938 p. 4
Maine Memory item 105266 and the NHHS map catalog offer routes to the 1859 Waldo County map and Fox Islands detail.
Waldo County and North Haven Maine

Books and Maps; Item 105266; NHHS 1859 map listing; https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/shop.html; accessed 2026-10-14
Map labels not inspected; do not assign parcels or owners from the catalog.

Columbia Daily Spectator May 16 1930; Article IDs cs19300516-01.2.6 and cs19310120-01.2.20; https://archive-publications.library.columbia.edu/?a=d&d=cs19300516-01.2.6; accessed 2026-10-14

Both issue pages blocked; search descriptions are not sufficient proof.

The Radcliffe News digitized volume; IA radcliffenews00collgoog; https://archive.org/details/radcliffenews00collgoog; accessed 2026-10-14

inventories.name: Offline and Paywalled Records
rows: What do the earliest surviving family entries actually say about Thomas, Mercy, Albert and Olive?
DAR GRC ME S2 V3 pp. 316–317; ME S2 V17 p. 1; American Ancestors MSS C403
DAR Library photocopy request form LG-3001; 202-879-3306 for questions. American Ancestors manuscript reference service via catalog route in the index.

Please provide the complete Beverage family Bible transcripts, title pages, ownership history and any original-page images for these exact references. Please confirm whether Olive is read as Carver or Carter.

DAR page lists GRC photocopy service: $10 member / $20 nonmember for up to 10 pages, $2 each additional page, $5 shipping. Record-copy applications are a separate $15 service effective March 16, 2026. Confirm current charges.
Secondary index only; underlying pages not accessed
Which conveyances underlie the two historical registrations?
Knox deed book 495 p. 361 and book 164 p. 370; registry 63-018 Sheep and 63-019 Little
Knox Registry of Deeds, 62 Union Street, Rockland ME 04841; 207-594-0422. Use registry index or ask staff for historical book/page copies.

Please provide the complete instruments and marginal references at 495/361 and 164/370. We need execution and recording dates, grantors, grantees, descriptions, prior-title references and adjoining owners. Historical research only; no current owner search.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Was the 1837 date execution, recording, an estate transaction or another Thomas?
Hancock deeds DGS 8296915, image 207 of 601, p. 387; Thomas Beverage to James Beverage and others, cited 28 June 1837
FamilySearch catalog or Hancock Registry of Deeds; use exact digital film, then confirm book from title frame.

Please supply the complete deed including preceding/following pages and volume title, with execution, acknowledgment and recording clauses. Thomas in the family baseline died 1834; please do not assume the indexed date was execution.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Which James married each woman, and who were the mothers of Susannah, Mary and Jane?
Marblehead marriages 1723, 1730 and 7 February 1733/4; Essex deeds 1788–1790 involving Susannah, Mary and Jane Beverage/Beveredge
Marblehead town vital records and Essex Southern District Registry of Deeds; published note lacks book/page.
Please locate the original marriage entries and grantor/grantee references for the unmarried Beverage sisters in 1789, including references to Sarah Holman and any deceased parent.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
North Haven vital records and stones
Which conflicting exact dates are correct?
Benjamin C. death December 7/17 1875; Charles H. birth 1862/1863; Sarah Sally death November 23/28 1844; Amelia death February 16 1908
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form. Ask town clerk for historical vital-entry access.

Please provide stone photographs and original register entries for these individuals, including adjacent family entries and register title pages. We are comparing conflicting transcriptions, not requesting changes.
NHHS states research help and copies/scans are free; donations welcome. Clerk/certified-copy fees not verified.
Which Sarah married Benjamin Kent, and which children belong to that couple?
Kent Cemetery Sarah d. 23 November 1821; Vinalhaven town/vital DGS 7596929 pp. 380, 389, 431, 433; Hancock deed DGS 7834663 p. 206 image 420/616, 24 April 1793
FamilySearch catalog and town clerk; inspect original records and marriage chronology.
Please provide Sarah Kent’s stone and the Kent family register entries and 1793 deed, including all spouse/parent wording. Distinguish Sarah born about 1758 from Thomas’s daughter born 1785.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Is December 31, 1780 baptism rather than birth, and are the stated parents correct?
Edgartown church baptism 31 December 1780; Dartmouth marriage intention 6 November 1766 for Benjamin Daggett and Elizabeth Hathaway
Edgartown and Dartmouth town/church archival records; institution to identify exact register.
Please supply the baptism entry and surrounding family baptisms, plus the parents’ marriage intention and any actual marriage record. We need birth and baptism kept distinct.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Was Eliot born in Massachusetts, who was Dorothy, and which degrees did he receive?
Eliot/Elliot Pierson Beverage/Beveridge, born 1908, died 1982; Harvard early 1930s; marriage before 1954

North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form. Harvard University Archives reference service; Massachusetts birth index then original entry.

Please identify Eliot’s family file, obituary, marriage reference and Harvard alumni/class entry. The family baseline uses Elliot and North Haven birthplace; museum biography uses Eliot and Massachusetts.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
What company records, plans, advertisements and photographs survive?
IsleBuilt circa 1955–1957; Penobscot Boat Works Rockport; Hopkins Store grain shed; Robbins-donated boat
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please identify IsleBuilt accession files, model drawings, advertisements, correspondence, employee captions and the donated boat catalog record. Please quote permission and high-resolution scan requirements.
NHHS research and scans stated free, donations welcome; reproduction permission still required.
What exactly does the contemporary death notice report, and does any source support the poisoning tradition?
Lime Rock Gazette 26 December 1850; Digital Maine article 1221; adjacent issues December 1850–January 1851
Maine State Library Digital Maine newspaper reference; use issue permalink.
Please provide a full-page scan and citation for the James and Lucy Beverage notice, plus related reports. We require exact wording and distinguish death notices from any explanation of cause.
Download returned 403; original issue not viewed
What is the earliest identifiable source of the existing participation claim?
Captain Thomas Beverage; family papers, descendants genealogy, commemorative records and any archival references underlying recognition

North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form. Use the existing site’s cited family-history trail and museum research inquiry route once an exact item is identified.

Please identify the earliest manuscript or published statement connecting Capt. Thomas Beverage to the Boston Tea Party, and provide a copy with provenance. The existing family claim will remain unchanged while evidence is assessed.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Where is the manuscript underlying Baxter volume XXI pages 221–222?
Thomas Beverage sworn statement, Fox Island, 1 June 1786; Robert Duglass fishing pass; William Vinal JP
Maine Historical Society manuscript reference; request crosswalk from Baxter printed page to manuscript collection.
Please identify and reproduce the original affidavit and related petition, including endorsements and docketing. Please supply collection, box/folder and item number.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Which estates establish family relationships and farm transfers?
John W. Beverage 1841–1875, possible case 1450 September 1876; Benjamin C. 1875; Albert 1888; Amelia 1908; Frank 1958
Knox Probate Court, 62 Union Street, Rockland ME 04841; 207-594-0427; probate@knoxcountymaine.gov. Confirm county jurisdiction before ordering early cases.

Please check probate indexes and provide docket numbers and inventories, wills, administrations and distributions for these deceased people. Case 1450 is an unverified memorial-page lead, not an established identifier.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Old Barn Hill chain of title
What instrument supports Frank’s reported 1880 inheritance and the 1819 house date?
Frank Beverage; Albert and Olive; Old Barn Hill Middle Road; backward title tracing from historical deeds and estate files

Knox Registry of Deeds, 62 Union Street, Rockland ME 04841; 207-594-0422. Use registry index or ask staff for historical book/page copies. North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please identify historic parcel descriptions and deeds/estate distributions supporting the 1880 inheritance claim, and the source for construction in 1819. Avoid supplying new private present-day owner information.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Blue Point Sky Farm and Carr estate
How do the farms connect through actual conveyances?
Alvin/Marion Beverage to Norton/Cheston; John H./Cora Beverage to Lamont; Benjamin Kent Beverage and Carr estate hypothesis
Knox Registry of Deeds, 62 Union Street, Rockland ME 04841; 207-594-0422. Use registry index or ask staff for historical book/page copies.

Please search historical grantor/grantee indexes for these named transfers, obtain all referenced prior deeds, and distinguish Blue Point, Sky Farm, Carr Point and Beveridge Point rather than treating them as the same parcel.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Do plans show earlier farm boundaries, buildings or owners?
Olmsted job 06653 Thomas W. Lamont North Haven 1918–1921; Corliss Lamont The Thomas Lamonts in America (1971) pp. 103, 142
Frederick Law Olmsted National Historic Site archival research service; job number supplied.

Please provide job 06653 drawing and correspondence inventory, dates, sheet numbers and reproduction options. Please distinguish archive evidence from later research notes quoting a user-created genealogy.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
What additional everyday family activity is documented?
Calderwood diaries; years 1925, 1933, 1940, 1951, partial 1958 and 1967 screened; remaining years and original pages not examined
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please identify the original pages for April 20, 1940 and January 21, 1958, and any complete diary index. We seek Beverage/Beveridge, initials, wives and farm names. Please explain permission requirements before excerpts are published.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Can the portrait be licensed and exact appointment dates clarified?
Columbia University Archives Historical Photographs Box 9 Beveridge Lowell Pierson; Spectator May 16 1930 article 01.2.6 and January 20 1931 article 01.2.20
Columbia University Libraries University Archives reference; use item 7250 and issue links.

Please provide the portrait metadata and high-resolution licensing terms, plus scans of the two Spectator articles and relevant appointment records. Faculty and chapel job titles must remain separate.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Does Lowell’s manuscript survive and is it cataloged?
Universal Harmony, roughly 2000 pages, reported at Virginia Theological Seminary in 1991
Virginia Theological Seminary library and archives reference service; present catalog locator unknown.
The 1991 diocesan journal p. 73 says Lowell P. Beveridge’s Universal Harmony manuscript was at the seminary. Please confirm custody, collection/call number, extent, access and copying terms.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Is there an eighth child missing from the baseline?
Orris Lyford and Rose Emma Pierson household census 1900–1920; Massachusetts births; Lyford Beveridge named in Lowell 1991 memorial
Historical censuses and Massachusetts vital records; original images not searched record by record.

Please compare all household members and children born/living counts, then obtain the birth or obituary record identifying Lyford’s parents. Do not infer a relationship solely from an obituary survivor line.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Which places and relatives can actually be identified in the film?
Islands of Maine circa 1930s; NHHS video catalog; original Harold Beverage 16mm film
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please supply film accession, original reel dates, digitization/edit history, shot list and permission terms. Are any shots positively documented as Beveridge Point, the red cottage or family members? We will not infer identity from appearance alone.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
What are accession numbers, dates and rights for family images?
Hiram hay rake 1917; Frank ox circa 1900; Sunday School circa 1912; Hanford barrel; Arthur farm cart; IsleBuilt boat
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please identify each item’s accession, donor, original caption, photographer/date, digitization master and rights holder. Please provide written permission and required credit for possible family-history website use.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Which James and Samuel held the named lots and office?
Town meeting 9 May 1764; James lot 7 (1758); Samuel lot 3 (1752); Pejepscot proprietor records
Topsham town archival records and Pejepscot historical/proprietor collections; exact call number not yet established.
Please provide the original election entry and grants or transfers for lots 7 and 3, including neighbors, occupations and family relationships. Two James profiles need separation.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Do military files verify units and establish parentage?
Alton T. Beverage 1917–1965; Edward M. Beverage 1915–1960; Samuel Hiram 1917–2014; chronologically eligible earlier men
National Archives/NPRC and historical draft/service collections; request by full name and life dates, without publishing sensitive identifiers.
Please identify available draft, discharge and service records, including name variants. Cemetery unit wording and family obituaries are leads, not substitutes for service files.
Not verified; archival status and copying fees must be confirmed
Where did each historical household live and what work or acreage was recorded?
Person queue; 1790–1950 population censuses; relevant Maine/Massachusetts state, mortality, agriculture and manufacturing schedules
National Archives, FamilySearch and state archival catalogs; historical record search, no modern people-finder services.

For each historical household, capture exact census year, place, ED/page/line, household members, occupation, land values where historical, and image citation. Record negative searches with the exact enumeration scope.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
What citations and family images do local books preserve?
The Colony (Lowell P. Beveridge Jr., 2015); The North Island (Norwood Beveridge, 1976); Pulpit Harbor Two Hundred Years; Silent Fingers of Faith; White Schoolhouses
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please confirm availability for consultation or interlibrary loan, and whether indexes or relevant Beverage pages can be copied for research with permission. We need citations and provenance behind claims.
Catalog lists The Colony $20 out of stock; The North Island $20; Pulpit Harbor $15; Silent Fingers $15; White Schoolhouses $15. Prices checked 2026-10-14; confirm availability.
Catalog viewed only; books not read
Which historical Beverage residences and landowners are labeled?
Maine Memory item 105266 Waldo County map; North Haven inset; NHHS Fox Islands reproduction
Maine Historical Society/Maine Memory item inquiry and NHHS shop.
Please supply a legible high-resolution North Haven inset and map title/legend. Record map date, scale, proprietor labels and rights; map labels alone do not establish title.
NHHS catalog lists map reproduction $20; digital licensing not verified
Orris school appointments and Olive education
Which schools employed Orris and did Olive Amelia attend Radcliffe?
Dorchester principal before 1921; Colby class 1887; Radcliffe News identifier radcliffenews00collgoog
Boston city/school annual reports; Colby archives; Radcliffe/Harvard archives.
Please identify Orris’s named school and service dates and Olive’s student record with birth/parent corroboration. An isolated student name is insufficient.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Which notices survive beyond general web indexing?
Rockland Courier Gazette, Lime Rock Gazette, Lewiston papers, Boston and Marblehead papers; 2–5 year windows around each event
Digital Maine, newspaper library microfilm and subscription databases using authorized access only.
Search Beverage/Beveridge/Beveredge/Beverege and initials, maiden/married/widow forms; include farm, vessel and business names. Return issue, page, column and image, not just OCR snippets.
Database or microfilm fees not verified
No comprehensive newspaper database sweep completed
How do farms and businesses change over time?
Historical North Haven/Vinalhaven tax books and valuation lists; directories for Hanford, Frank, Fremont, Hiram and IsleBuilt
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form. Town historical records; historical directories through libraries.
Please identify surviving historic tax and valuation books and business directories, especially transfer years. Do not provide newly discovered present-day private addresses or financial details.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
What do church membership, pew and contribution records show?
Pulpit Harbor Baptist Society 1867 onward; bell gift October/November 1896; Lowell piano 1925
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form. Ask society to identify church records custodian.
Please identify membership, baptism, marriage, pew ownership and bell-donation entries involving Beverage relatives, and any original photograph or copy of the bell inscription.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
Maritime customs vessel and casualty records
Can vessel connections be established independently?
Ann about 30 tons circa 1781; steamer Tremont 1896 delivery; lost-at-sea William Beverage and Malcolm Crockett memorial wording
Maine maritime collections, customs district records and contemporary newspapers; exact series not yet identified.
Please search relevant vessel registers, clearances and casualty notices with owner/master and date corroboration. A repeated vessel name must not be assumed to be the same vessel.
Not published or not verified; request quotation
NHHS family vertical files, recovered road/bridge/school deeds, Lily Pond Ice Company papers; family correspondence and photograph donors
North Haven Historical Society, P.O. Box 322, 77 Pulpit Harbor Road, North Haven ME 04853; 207-867-4752; official contact form.

Please inventory Beverage/Beveridge and associated-family vertical files and identify the recovered road, bridge, school-deed and ice-company records mentioned in the society history. Request a box/folder list before selecting copies.
Not published or not verified; request quotation

inventories.name: Timeline
rows: James Beveridge Sr. was born around 1700, likely in Scotland (family tradition places his birth in Dunfermline, Fife). He later migrated to Marblehead, Massachusetts and became the patriarch of the Beverage family.
Albert and Thomas family Bible records
A secondary Bible directory points to DAR Maine series 2 volume 3 pages 316–317, series 2 volume 17 page 1, and NEHGS manuscript C403.
Marriage of James Beveridge Sr. and Sarah Bennett
James Beveridge Sr. married Sarah Bennett at St. Michael's Church in Marblehead, Massachusetts. This was his first marriage.
James Beveridge Jr. was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts. He later settled on the Fox Islands (North Haven) and married Jean McKinney White.
Sarah Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Sarah Bennett, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts. She later married Peter Ayers.
Sarah Holman and Mary White chronology

Sarah Holman’s stored birth date equals her marriage date. Mary White’s stored 1728 birth would make her about two at the recorded 1730 marriage; daughters born after her stored 1731 death also require review.
Marriage of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White
After the death of his first wife Sarah Bennett, James Beveridge Sr. married Mary White in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
The Essex Antiquarian reports a February 7, 1733/4 marriage, and Susannah, Mary and Jane living unmarried in Marblehead in 1789 after their mother Sarah’s death.
Marriage of James Beveridge Sr. and Sarah Holman
James Beveridge Sr. married his third wife, Sarah Holman, in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Susannah Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Jane Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Mary Beveridge, daughter of James Beveridge Sr. and Mary White, was born in Marblehead, Massachusetts.
Marriage of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White
James Beveridge Jr. married Jean (Jane) McKinney White, widow of Nicholas White, in Georgetown, Maine. This union linked the Beveridge and White families.

Capt. Thomas Beverage (born Thomas Beveridge) was born at Mere’s Point, Topsham, Maine, in a stockaded house built by Capt. John Minot. He would later become a privateer and town clerk of North Haven.
James and Samuel Beveridge Topsham lots
The early land-owner list places James Beveridge at lot 7 in 1758 and Samuel Beveridge at lot 3 in 1752.
Mercy Beveridge Henry, daughter of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White, was born. She later married Henry Henry.
Mercy Kent was born in Marshfield, Massachusetts. She married Capt. Thomas Beverage and settled on North Haven Island.
Sarah Beveridge Kent, daughter of James Beveridge Jr. and Jean McKinney White, was born. She later married Benjamin Kent, creating a double in-law tie between the Beveridge and Kent families.
Sarah Beverage Kent and Sarah Sally Beverage

The Kent cemetery transcription calls Sarah Beverage Kent, deceased November 23, 1821 aged 63 years 5 months, a sister of Capt. Thomas. She must not be merged with his daughter Sarah Sally, born 1785.
James Beverage elected at Topsham’s first town meeting

At Topsham’s first town meeting after incorporation, James Beverage was elected hog constable. The office was modest, but the record places the Beveridge/Beverage family inside the first formal municipal government of the town where the family lived before the Fox Islands generation.
Wheeler’s town history names James Beverage and William Alexander as hog constables elected at Topsham’s first town meeting, May 9, 1764.
The genealogy gives Diana parents Benjamin Daggett and Elizabeth Hathaway, husband Nathaniel Beverage, and one son and three daughters.

Family letters and deeds indicate that Capt. Thomas Beverage participated in the Boston Tea Party on 16 December 1773. He traveled from the Fox Islands to Marblehead and joined the group of patriots who destroyed tea in Boston Harbor.
Thomas sells 120 acres on North Fox Island

On 3 January 1774, Thomas Beveridge of Marblehead sold a 120-acre tract on North Fox Island to William Blackler for 53 pounds 13 shillings. The land bounded on William Perry’s land, a pond, Ezekiel Kent’s land and the thoroughfare.
Marriage of Thomas Beverage and Mercy Kent
Thomas Beverage married Mercy Kent at Trinity Church in Boston, Massachusetts. Mercy was the daughter of Ezekiel Kent and Susanna Bryant Winslow.
The Trinity Church published register records Thomas Beverege marrying Mercy Kent on April 13, 1774.
John White Beverage, eldest son of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He was named after Mercy’s son by her first husband John White.
Nathaniel Winslow Beverage, second son of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later became a deacon in Camden.
William Blackler reconveys land to Thomas
On 1 March 1779, William Blackler reconveyed the 120-acre tract on North Fox Island back to Thomas Beverage for £200. The land now measured 125 acres.
Benjamin Kent Beverage, third son of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He was named after his uncle Benjamin Kent.
The Doggett-Daggett genealogy identifies Diana’s December 31, 1780 event at Edgartown as baptism, while the repository stores it as birth.

On 9 March 1781, Thomas Beverage and Abigail Dyer witnessed David Woster Sr. transferring half of his North Haven land to his infant son David Woster Jr. for $500. The transaction was recorded in 1801.
Thomas Beverage testifies about Robert Duglase

In 1781, Thomas Beverage testified that Robert Duglase of Fox Island procured a pass from Capt. Henry Mowitt for fishing and bought a schooner from Billings Putnam of Newburyport. This testimony was recorded on 1 June 1786.
A published sworn statement places Thomas Beverage at Fox Island on June 1, 1786, testifying about a fishing pass he saw in 1781.
Schooner Ann and Thomas Beverage associates
Thomas’s testimony names Robert Duglass, Capt. Henry Mowit, Billings Putnam, Paul Reed and justice William Vinal, and describes a roughly 30-ton schooner Ann.
Mercy Kent Beverage, fourth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island.
Thomas sells 120 acres to Samuel Thomas
On 3 November 1784, Thomas Beverage sold 120 acres of land on North Fox Island to Samuel Thomas for 150 pounds. The land later came into Kent and Beverage hands.
Thomas purchases 100 acres from Nathaniel Crockett Jr.
Thomas Beverage purchased 100 acres on North Haven from Nathaniel Crockett Jr. This land later formed part of the family estate. The deed was registered in 1806.
Fox Islands petition for land titles

In March 1785, the inhabitants of the Fox Islands Plantation met at the home of Benjamin Kent and Sarah Beveridge Kent to petition the Massachusetts General Court for clear title to lands occupied before 1 June 1784. James Beveridge Sr. was chosen moderator and Thomas Beverage was elected Plantation Clerk.
Sarah ("Sally") Beverage, fifth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She later married Benjamin Kent.
Benjamin Kent junior and John Kent
Edited Woodruff biographies identify Benjamin Kent (1798–1882) and John Kent (1786–1874) as sons of Benjamin and Sarah Beverage, with spouses Deborah Thomas and Nancy Luce respectively.
Lydia Winslow Beverage, sixth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She died young in 1792.
On 21 May 1788, Thomas Beverage settled accounts with Abel Whitman, receiving payment in full for half of the island he had sold him.
Thomas Beverage registers his cattle mark
On 9 March 1789, Thomas Beverage registered his cattle mark in the town records: the left ear split and a half-penny out of the foreside of the right ear.
James Beverage, seventh child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later became a tanner and landowner.
Thomas Beverage begins nine-year run as Vinalhaven town clerk

Vinalhaven’s centennial office roster lists Thomas Beverage as town clerk every year from 1790 through 1798. He also appears among the selectmen in 1797, documenting sustained involvement in the island town’s early civil government.
1790 Census enumeration of the Beverage household

The 1790 U.S. Census recorded the household of Thomas Beverage on North Haven with two males over 16 (Thomas and John), four males under 16 (Nathaniel, Benjamin, James, Josiah) and five females (Mercy, Mercy Jr., Sarah, Lydia and an unknown female).

On 10 October 1791, Thomas Beverage and William Cooper witnessed James and Elizabeth Heard selling Pulpit Harbor land for 90 pounds. The land was near Samuel Lewis’s property.
On 27 March 1792, Thomas Beverage and Levi Smith witnessed Charles Stewart and Abel Whitman selling Eames Island (40 acres) to John Brooks for 30 pounds.
Josiah Winslow Beverage, eighth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later served as town selectman and co-owned the family mill.
On 6 April 1795, Thomas Beverage and his son Nathaniel Beverage witnessed Charles Stewart selling 38¾ acres to John Newbury.
Lydia Winslow Beverage, ninth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She died in 1829.
On 20 May 1796, Thomas Beverage and Cornelius Bramhall witnessed Levi Smith selling 50 acres to Thomas Cooper for $250.
Thomas sells land to William Vinal
On 18 April 1797, Thomas Beverage sold a parcel of land near the North Harbor to William Vinal of Vinalhaven for $4. The deed was witnessed by Gabriel Johonnot and George Ulmer.
The edited Benjamin Kent biography gives June 17, 1798 in its narrative and January 17 in a note; Fuller transcription gives June 17.
John Beverage succeeds Thomas as Vinalhaven town clerk
John Beverage appears as Vinalhaven town clerk in every annual roster from 1799 through 1812, a fourteen-year span immediately following Thomas Beverage’s nine-year tenure.
Witness to George White land sale
On 16 September 1800, Thomas Beverage and his son John White Beverage witnessed George White selling land by the Pond Swamp to Joseph Maddocks for $100.
NHHS preserves Frank’s recollection of buying island wool for the Knox Woolen Mill in Camden and supplies a photograph of him with an ox dated about 1900.
NHHS describes Alvin and Marion Beverage’s Blue Point farm passing to Nortons then Chestons, and John H. and Cora Beverage’s farm becoming the Lamont estate Sky Farm.
Abigail Beverage, tenth child of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She died the following day.
Abigail Beverage, infant daughter of Thomas and Mercy Beverage, died the day after her birth on North Haven Island.
Sale of mill shares to Henry Alexander
On 28 February 1806, Thomas Beverage sold Henry Alexander 1/8 share of the sawmill and 1/4 share of the grist mill for $300. The deed was witnessed by William Vinall and William Norwood.
Repurchase of land and mills from Henry Alexander
On 15 December 1807, Henry Alexander sold back to Thomas Beverage 115 acres, a dwelling house, barn, and shares in a sawmill and grist mill for $1500.
John Beverage joins protest over moving Hancock County courts

The Massachusetts House journal recorded a memorial from John Beverage and other inhabitants of Vinalhaven remonstrating against removal of the Hancock County courts from Castine to Buckstown. The petition shows island residents engaging directly with state government over access to county institutions.
Robert Henry sells 100 acres to Oliver Amsbury

On 17 February 1808, Robert Henry of Topsham sold 100 acres on North Haven to Oliver Amsbury of Vinalhaven for $350, reserving 60 acres previously conveyed to David Perry. The deed was witnessed by Thomas Beverage and David Wooster Jr.
Thomas sells 115 acres to Josiah and James
On 11 May 1811, Thomas Beverage sold 115 acres, a dwelling house, barn, and shares in a sawmill and grist mill to his sons Josiah Winslow Beverage and James Beverage for $2,500.
Sale of 12 acres to Cornelius Bramhall
On 17 April 1813, Thomas Beverage sold 12 acres on the northeast cove of North Harbor to Cornelius Bramhall for $150. The deed was witnessed by Sarah and Sally Bramhall.
Sale of land to Malatiah Luce and Jonathan Smith
On 23 January 1814, Thomas Beverage sold land at the head of the Mill Pond to Malatiah Luce and Jonathan Smith for $150. The deed was witnessed by John Wagg and Nathaniel Beverage.
Thomas Beverage appointed delegate to Brunswick convention
In September 1816, Thomas Beverage was selected by the town to serve as delegate to the convention at Brunswick to discuss the separation of Maine from Massachusetts.
Benjamin Beverage represents Vinalhaven at Maine’s Constitutional Convention
Benjamin Beverage was Vinalhaven’s delegate to the 1819 convention that framed the constitution for the new State of Maine as separation from Massachusetts approached.
Mercy Kent Beverage, wife of Capt. Thomas Beverage, died on North Haven Island.
Benjamin Beverage writes a history of Vinalhaven

A surviving ink manuscript by Benjamin Beverage, dated December 20, 1819 and now in the Maine Historical Society’s William D. Williamson papers, recounts Vinalhaven’s settlement, land distribution, vessels and religion. It provides a rare first-hand historical voice from a member of the family.
NHHS describes a house on Old Barn Hill built in 1819 and a farm inherited by Frank in 1880.
Marriage of James Beverage and Jemima Crabtree
James Beverage married Jemima Crabtree on North Haven Island. Their union connected the Beverage family with the Crabtrees, another prominent island family.
Benjamin Crabtree Beverage, eldest son of James Beverage and Jemima Crabtree, was born on North Haven Island.
Benjamin Beverage serves in the Maine House
The State of Maine’s 1823 civil-government record lists Benjamin Beverage as representative for Vinalhaven together with a long group of neighboring islands.
Harrison Beverage, second son of James and Jemima Beverage, was born on North Haven Island.
Albert Glover Beverage, third son of James and Jemima Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. He later became a deacon and farmer.
Nathaniel Beverage represents Vinalhaven in the Maine House
The official 1828 Maine House payroll lists Nathaniel Beverage as the representative from Vinalhaven, extending the family’s documented participation from island offices into state government.
Lucy C. Beverage, only daughter of James and Jemima Beverage, was born on North Haven Island. She later died in 1850 after exposure to mercury in her father’s tannery.
Two repository IDs appear to describe the same wife of Benjamin Crabtree and daughter of Norwood and Hannah; birth dates differ January 31 versus January 1, 1833.
Capt. Thomas Beverage died on North Haven Island. His grave is marked with a title recognizing his service during the Revolutionary War.
A Woodruff biography cites a Thomas Beverage to James Beverage and others deed under June 28, 1837, after Thomas’s repository death in 1834.
Jemima Crabtree Beverage died on North Haven Island, likely from a hemorrhage linked to mercurial poisoning from the tannery.
Woodruff’s April 3, 1838 diary transcription records an afternoon visit to Josiah Devrage; project editors identify him as Josiah Beverage.
Seaview gives Sarah death November 23, 1844 aged 59 years 8 months, versus repository November 28.
Maine authorizes a Pulpit Harbor toll bridge to Beverage family land

A Maine act established the North Haven Bridge Company and authorized a toll bridge over the head of Pulpit Harbor from Enos Cooper’s land to land belonging to James and Josiah Beverage. The law required a bridge at least twelve feet wide and a draw to allow vessels to pass. The act proves the property relationship and proposed infrastructure; it does not by itself prove that the bridge was ultimately built.
James Beverage died on North Haven Island. His death, and that of his daughter Lucy two days later, were attributed to mercury poisoning from his tannery.
Lucy C. Beverage, daughter of James and Jemima Beverage, died two days after her father due to mercury poisoning from the tannery.
A Digital Maine search points to James and Lucy Beverage death notices in the Lime Rock Gazette of December 26, 1850.
Benjamin Kent Beverage died on North Haven Island at age 72.
Marriage of Benjamin Crabtree Beverage and Amelia Beverage
After his divorce from Sarah W. Loveland, Benjamin Crabtree Beverage married his second cousin Amelia Beverage on North Haven Island.
Harrison Beverage chosen as a representative

Vinalhaven's published town history records that Harrison Beverage of North Haven was chosen as a representative in 1859 and later resigned; Lewis Leadbetter was elected in his place at a December special meeting.
Maine Memory item 105266 and the NHHS map catalog offer routes to the 1859 Waldo County map and Fox Islands detail.

Seaview gives Benjamin C. death December 17, 1875, versus repository December 7.

Albert G. Beverage listed as a representative

Marriage of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Margaret Leadbetter
Samuel Carver Beverage married Ruth Margaret Leadbetter in a double wedding on North Haven. Ruth’s brother Isaac Leadbetter married Jennie Sawyer at the same ceremony.

Orris Lyford Beverage graduates from Colby while leading a high school

Colby University’s 1887 catalogue places Orris Lyford Beverage in the graduating class and identifies him as principal of the high school at Hallowell, documenting the start of the education career later associated with him.
Marriage of Orris Lyford Beverage and Rose Emma Pierson
Orris Lyford Beverage married Rose Emma Pierson at Tenants Harbor, Maine. Their marriage produced eight children.
