A digitized Radcliffe News volume may contain a relevant Olive Beveridge student reference.
NHHS cites Fremont’s 1901 superintendent report in its account of the island high school.
Wilson Freemont Beverage, son of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island.
Alma Marie Beverage, daughter of Samuel Carver Beverage and Ruth Leadbetter, was born on North Haven Island. She died in infancy.
The diocesan memorial prints 1905-09-19 to 1991-06-18 but calls Lowell 86; those dates yield 85. It calls him a Boston native, while the repository retains North Haven birthplace.
Birth of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage
Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage was born in Dorchester, Massachusetts. He later became a minister and father of Albion Pierson Beverage III.
NHHS names Elsie, Jennie and Linda Beverage among the first 1907 high school graduates and Nettie Beverage Crockett as class of 1912.
The repository calls him Elliot Pierson Beverage born North Haven; NHHS calls him Eliot Beveridge born Massachusetts in 1908.
Seaview gives Amelia’s death as February 16, 1908 aged 75 years 12 days; its birth column incorrectly repeats 1908.
Frank Beverage joins North Haven petition to Congress

The Congressional Record lists Frank Beverage and other North Haven residents among petitioners asking Congress to pass the Kenyon-Sheppard interstate liquor bill, showing direct participation in a nationally contested Progressive Era policy issue.
Teenage Harold Beverage receives Carpathia wireless signals after Titanic disaster

IEEE’s institutional biography reports that Harold Beverage, already experimenting with a homemade wireless station as a teenager, picked up signals from Carpathia, the ship that rescued survivors of the Titanic disaster. The episode foreshadowed the long-distance radio work that later made his name internationally known.
A circa 1912 NHHS photograph caption identifies Jennie Beverage, Nettie Crockett, Etta Beverage and Olive Gregory among Mrs. Watts’s class.
Harold Beverage graduates from the University of Maine
Harold H. Beverage completed his electrical-engineering degree at the University of Maine in 1915 before beginning his engineering career with General Electric.
A Maine state year-book entry for North Haven lists Fremont Beverage as school superintendent and gives February 25, 1915 as the date associated with his service as a justice.
Alton T and Edward M Beverage military inscriptions
Fuller transcription lists Alton T. Beverage, March 23, 1917–November 20, 1965, with Tec4 734 WWII, and Edward M., December 15, 1915–March 5, 1960, with PFC 346 Ord Med Maint Co WWII.
Elmira Carver Beverage and Isa Beverage
NHHS identifies Elmira as Isa’s mother and associates them with the store at the end of Beach Bridge.
Marriage of Hiram Stone Beverage and Ruby Hazel Taylor
Hiram Stone Beverage married Ruby Hazel Taylor around 1916 on North Haven Island. They had one son, Samuel Hiram Beverage.
Samuel Hiram Beverage, only child of Hiram Stone Beverage and Ruby Hazel Taylor, was born at Sunnyside farm on North Haven Island.
Hiram Beverage farm equipment and images
The museum guide identifies Hiram on a hay rake in a 1917 photograph and describes poultry crates made in winter 1933–1934.
NPS research notes point to Olmsted job 06653 for Thomas W. Lamont at North Haven, 1918–1921, and a Carr Point newspaper reference of May 16, 1938.
Harold Beverage receives radio receiving-system patent
U.S. Patent 1,381,089 was issued to Harold H. Beverage for a directional radio receiving system after an application filed on April 10, 1920. The patent was assigned to General Electric Company.
Harold Beverage receives the Liebmann Memorial Prize
The Institute of Radio Engineers recognized Harold Beverage with its Morris N. Liebmann Memorial Prize for his contributions to transoceanic radio and directional antennas.
A Calderwood entry records Lowell Beverage playing piano at church on August 9, 1925.
Frank Beverage calls North Haven water-loan bonds as town treasurer

A contemporary Courier-Gazette notice signed by Frank Beverage as North Haven treasurer called a numbered group of municipal water-loan bonds for payment effective September 1, 1926. The notice documents his responsibility for the town’s public finance and water infrastructure debt.
Frank Beverage serves as auctioneer for Pulpit Harbor property sale

A Courier-Gazette advertisement announced the public sale of the Sands H. Witherspoon homestead at Pulpit Harbor and named Frank Beverage as auctioneer, documenting another aspect of his local business and community role.
Marriage of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Elizabeth Reed
Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage married Grace Elizabeth Reed in Dorchester, Massachusetts. They later raised their family in Dresden, Maine.
The fraternity’s 1928 history lists Orris Lyford Beverage, Colby class of 1887, as a deceased school principal at Dorchester.
Nancy Beverage, daughter of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Reed, was born. She later lived in Maine.
The May 16, 1930 and January 20, 1931 Spectator items are specific retrieval targets for Lowell’s early appointments and choir work.
Columbia catalog item 7250 identifies a Lowell Pierson Beveridge portrait in University Archives Historical Photographs Box 9.
NHHS catalogs Islands of Maine, a circa 1930s film made from Harold Beverage’s 16mm footage of North Haven, Vinalhaven and Rockland, edited by Tim Trevaskis.
Hiram Beverage builds the Mill Stream dam

Two independent local-history accounts identify Hiram “Hightie” Beverage as the builder of the present Mill Stream dam in 1932. The resulting brackish pond became known locally as Hightie's Pond and later supported oyster aquaculture.
Grace Pauline Beverage, daughter of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Reed, was born.
Harold Beverage serves as IRE president
Harold H. Beverage served as president of the Institute of Radio Engineers in 1937.
Columbia’s chapel history gives Lowell’s organist and director of chapel music tenure as 1937–1952, distinct from his broader 1930–1952 faculty service.
Birth of Albion Pierson Beverage III
Albion Pierson Beverage III, son of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage and Grace Elizabeth Reed, was born (approximate date). He later maintained the family cottage on North Haven.
Janice Lynn Marshall (later Beverage) was born around 1940. She married Albion Pierson Beverage III around 1962 and was the family genealogist.
Nettie Beverage and Malcolm Crockett marriage
The April 20, 1940 Calderwood entry says Malcolm Crockett and Nettie Beverage married the previous evening, indicating April 19.
Gerald G. Beverage enters U.S. Navy service in World War II

Gerald Beverage entered the U.S. Navy in December 1942 after completing Yale Law School. His obituary reports Pacific Theater service connected with campaigns at Kwajalein, Saipan, Guam, the Philippines and Iwo Jima, and says he left active service in late 1945 as a lieutenant. The timeline deliberately omits an obituary ship-name detail that has not yet been independently verified.
Samuel Hiram Beverage departs for overseas Signal Corps service

Samuel Beverage’s detailed obituary reports that he sailed from New York on July 16, 1942 and subsequently served as a Master Sergeant and Radio/Communications Chief with the 1060th Signal Company, 323rd Air Service Group across Libya, Tunisia, Egypt, Lebanon, Palestine and Italy through May 1945.
Harold Beverage receives the IRE Medal of Honor
The Institute of Radio Engineers awarded Harold H. Beverage its Medal of Honor in recognition of his radio research, inventions, practical engineering work, and service to the institute.
Marriage of Samuel Hiram Beverage and Eleanor Mae Sargent
Samuel Hiram Beverage married Eleanor Mae Sargent in Somerville, Massachusetts in 1945. They raised five children and were instrumental in preserving North Haven history.
Death of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage
Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage died in Silver Spring, Maryland at age 43. He was buried in Fuller Cemetery on North Haven Island.
John Miller Beverage begins missionary service in Guatemala

After completing Dallas Theological Seminary in 1953, John Miller Beverage was appointed by Central American Mission and served as a missionary in Guatemala until 1972 before returning to work at Dallas Theological Seminary.
Eliot and Dorothy return to North Haven
NHHS says Eliot and wife Dorothy returned permanently in 1954; January 1958 diary entries name both in island social and work activities.
NHHS identifies Eliot Beveridge as the founder of IsleBuilt in 1955, making boats on North Haven circa 1955–1957 with Penobscot Boat Works in Rockport.
NHHS lists Sport-O-Ramic, Skim-Skiff and Skim-Fisher models, more than 350 boats and more than ten winter workers; production used the Hopkins Store grain shed.
Death of Ruth Margaret Leadbetter Beverage
Ruth Margaret Leadbetter Beverage died on North Haven Island at age 92, having raised twelve children.
Harold Beverage retires from RCA leadership
Harold Beverage retired in 1958 from his RCA Communications research-and-development leadership and radio-research directorship, then continued working as a communications consultant.
The Calderwood diary records hauling about five cords from Beveridge’s Point for Eliot Beveridge on January 21, 1958, assisted by Berger Yonquist.
Seaview transcription gives Frank’s death as May 16, 1958 and identifies wife May U. Calderwood.
Marriage of Albion Pierson Beverage III and Janice Marshall
Albion Pierson Beverage III married Janice Lynn Marshall around 1962. They celebrated over 60 years of marriage and preserved the family cottage on North Haven.
Death of Ruby Hazel Taylor Beverage
Ruby Hazel Taylor Beverage, wife of Hiram Stone Beverage and mother of Samuel Hiram Beverage, died on North Haven Island.
Robert Elliot Beverage, son of Albion Pierson Beverage III and Janice Marshall, was born (approximate date). He later married Heather Beverage and co-owns property on North Haven.

Samuel Beverage returns to North Haven and helps establish its historical society

After retiring back to North Haven in 1973, Samuel Hiram Beverage worked with Lewis and Ida Haskell in efforts that his obituary credits as instrumental in establishing the North Haven Historical Society, linking his later life directly to preservation of island history.
Founding of North Haven Historical Society
After returning permanently to North Haven in 1973, Samuel Hiram Beverage and his wife Eleanor helped found the North Haven Historical Society to preserve island history.
In 1974, Arthur Walter Beverage Sr., a great-great-grandson of Capt. Thomas Beverage, sold Old Barn Hill to Henry Meigs. The hill was later developed as a private residence.
Eliot and Sam NHHS founding work
The society’s history names Eliot Beverage vice president at the June 27, 1976 organization and credits Sam with recovering threatened town records.

A 2010 OCU law review tribute records Norwood’s arrival in 1989, academic deanship, faculty governance and teaching at Nankai University.

Robert Elliot Beverage and Heather Beverage purchased a home at 128 S Orchard Street in Wallingford, Connecticut, where they raised their family.
Death of Grace Elizabeth Reed Beverage
Grace Elizabeth Reed Beverage, widow of Rev. Albion Pierson Beverage, died in Dresden, Maine at age 99.
Samuel H. Beverage receives North Haven's Boston Post Cane
North Haven awarded its Boston Post Cane to Samuel H. Beverage on December 4, 2010, two days before his ninety-third birthday, recognizing him as the town's oldest resident.
A 2012 Brooklyn Historical Society interview preserves Pete Beveridge’s recollections of childhood summers with his family on the Maine island.
Samuel Hiram Beverage died on North Haven Island at age 97. He was a radio enthusiast, WWII veteran, and co-founder of the North Haven Historical Society.
Norwood Pierson Beveridge Jr. dies during the COVID-19 pandemic

Norwood P. Beveridge Jr., a Harvard-trained attorney and longtime law professor, died on October 31, 2020. His published obituary explicitly identifies COVID-19 as the cause of death, making his death a documented family connection to the global pandemic.
Death of Janice Lynn Marshall Beverage
Janice Lynn Marshall Beverage died in Ocala, Florida after a long life dedicated to her family and genealogy research.

The 2024 North Haven tax commitment list recorded Albion Pierson Beverage III and Robert E. Beverage as co-owners of parcel 13-004-D at 216 Beverage Colony Road, continuing the family’s land ownership on the island.

rows: Vinalhaven’s centennial office roster lists Thomas Beverage as town clerk every year from 1790 through 1798. He also appears among the selectmen in 1797, documenting sustained involvement in the island town’s early civil government.

Vinalhaven’s centennial office roster lists Thomas Beverage as town clerk every year from 1790 through 1798. He also appears among the selectmen in 1797, documenting sustained involvement in the island town’s early civil government.
John Beverage appears as Vinalhaven town clerk in every annual roster from 1799 through 1812, a fourteen-year span immediately following Thomas Beverage’s nine-year tenure.

inventories.name: Baseline Research Notes
rows: Structured repository audit plus source review

Every birth, death, and timeline date was parsed and inventoried. Legacy values ending in January 1 were compared with their cited source descriptions and prioritized for direct-record searches. Where no reviewed source explicitly established January 1, the original stored value remains available for provenance while the public display now shows only the supported year. Exact replacements are limited to dates directly stated by reviewed sources.
The timeline no longer turns a known year into a fictional New Year's Day. Exact, year-only, approximate, and unknown values now sort consistently and display honestly.

The Kennebec Journal obituary states that Grace was born to Robert George Reed and Annie MacKinnon Reed on October 31, 1909 in Boston and died June 7, 2008 at her son's home in Pittsfield. It supplies two full dates and a much richer life history while exposing a place-and-age conflict for family review rather than silently erasing the earlier narrative.

Tier 2 institutional archive plus Tier 3 contemporary obituary

Lowell Beveridge was a Harvard-trained musicologist, organist, conductor, educator, and Episcopal priest. Columbia University documents his 1930–1952 faculty service, university-organist role, and efforts to strengthen its music collections. His obituary traces later service at Union Theological Seminary and Virginia Theological Seminary and records his death on June 18, 1991.
A previously skeletal profile now has exact life dates and a documented multi-institution career.
The existing profile says North Haven as birthplace; published references say Boston or Dorchester. The existing place remains pending a birth record.

A systematic pass over the 180-profile archive targeted historical substance rather than new relationships. Strong discoveries include the Beverage family’s multigenerational Vinalhaven town-office service; Benjamin Beverage’s 1819 constitutional-convention role, surviving history manuscript and 1823 Maine House service; Nathaniel Beverage’s 1828 House service; the 1848 Pulpit Harbor bridge authorization adjoining James and Josiah Beverage land; Orris Beverage’s Colby/education record; Frank Beverage’s town-finance, auction and federal-petition activity; Harold Beverage’s early Carpathia wireless episode; and richer military, professional, missionary, maritime and community histories for twentieth-century relatives.
The archive now shows what family members did and how they interacted with island, state, national and world events instead of presenting most people only as names and dates.
Obtain original military service files for Samuel Hiram Beverage and Gerald Gibson Beverage
Resolve Civil War sailor-index leads for Edgar, Lyford and Nathan Beverage before attaching service claims
Find primary death evidence for the Benjamin Crabtree Beverage diphtheria tradition

Search additional unindexed Rockland/Belfast newspaper runs for island accidents, maritime incidents and court cases

The inherited timeline attributes Jemima Crabtree Beverage’s 1837 death and the December 1850 deaths of James Beverage and daughter Lucy C. Beverage to mercury or mercurial exposure associated with James’s tannery. The current base entries ultimately cite a Find a Grave memorial. Targeted searches were run for the three people, North Haven/Vinalhaven, tannery/tanning, mercury/mercurial/quicksilver, hemorrhage and poisoning variants, including historical newspapers and the 1889 Vinalhaven history. No independent contemporaneous or official source establishing mercury poisoning was located in this pass.

This is a memorable family story and therefore especially important to label honestly. The archive preserves the tradition but no longer presents the poisoning mechanism as if it had already been independently verified.

Sarah Holman and Mary White chronology

BF-R005 Sarah Holman’s stored birth date equals her marriage date. Mary White’s stored 1728 birth would make her about two at the recorded 1730 marriage; daughters born after her stored 1731 death also require review.
BF-R008 The Doggett-Daggett genealogy identifies Diana’s December 31, 1780 event at Edgartown as baptism, while the repository stores it as birth.
BF-R011 A Woodruff biography cites a Thomas Beverage to James Beverage and others deed under June 28, 1837, after Thomas’s repository death in 1834.
Sarah Beverage Kent and Sarah Sally Beverage

BF-R012 The Kent cemetery transcription calls Sarah Beverage Kent, deceased November 23, 1821 aged 63 years 5 months, a sister of Capt. Thomas. She must not be merged with his daughter Sarah Sally, born 1785.
BF-R014 The edited Benjamin Kent biography gives June 17, 1798 in its narrative and January 17 in a note; Fuller transcription gives June 17.
BF-R032 The repository calls him Elliot Pierson Beverage born North Haven; NHHS calls him Eliot Beveridge born Massachusetts in 1908.
BF-R039 The diocesan memorial prints 1905-09-19 to 1991-06-18 but calls Lowell 86; those dates yield 85. It calls him a Boston native, while the repository retains North Haven birthplace.
BF-R046 Seaview lists Charles H. as 1862–1938, versus repository birth year 1863.
BF-R047 Seaview gives Benjamin C. death December 17, 1875, versus repository December 7.
BF-R048 Seaview gives Sarah death November 23, 1844 aged 59 years 8 months, versus repository November 28.
BF-R049 Two repository IDs appear to describe the same wife of Benjamin Crabtree and daughter of Norwood and Hannah; birth dates differ January 31 versus January 1, 1833.

blocks.text: Beverage Family Research Dossier
Evidence and proposed additions for family review

This collection adds a documented research layer to the Beverage Family website baseline. It identifies historical records, images, businesses and family connections that deserve attention, while preserving uncertain identifications and conflicting dates. The repository itself is an index of hypotheses, not independent proof.

This is a substantial first research volume, not a declaration that every archive has been exhausted. Original deeds, probate packets, family Bible pages, most census schedules and many vital records remain to be obtained. The accompanying gaps plan specifies those retrievals rather than guessing their contents.

Sources examined counts 56 distinct content or catalog records directly inspected, including transcriptions and institutional descriptions. It excludes inherited citations not rechecked and blocked snippet-only targets. The 18 strong new discoveries include confirmed catalog or museum attributions; they are not 18 independently proved genealogical relationships. The five corroborating source entries are useful additions but must not automatically be counted as independent witnesses.

All 180 repository people are indexed. Name searches were run for 154 historical or known-deceased profiles; 26 living or unresolved-status profiles were deferred from new personal research. A second engine pass covered 115 earlier profiles. General name searches do not substitute for a record-by-record census, newspaper or courthouse investigation.

The read-only baseline is commit 4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1. It contains 127 merged events and 21 structured places. No repository file, website content, branch, commit or pull request was changed. The existing Boston Tea Party claim and relative address/property fields remain unchanged. [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)
1. Thomas Beverage — BF-R001 — Probable
2. Arnold P Beveridge island registrations — BF-R033 — Confirmed
3. Eliot Beveridge and IsleBuilt — BF-R028 — Strongly supported
4. Nettie Beverage and Malcolm Crockett marriage — BF-R025 — Strongly supported
5. Albert and Thomas family Bible records — BF-R052 — Possible lead
6. James Beveredge and Sarah Holman — BF-R004 — Probable
7. Diana Daggett family cluster — BF-R009 — Probable
8. Lowell Beveridge portrait — BF-R035 — Confirmed
9. Harold Beverage films — BF-R043 — Confirmed
10. Alvin Beverage and church bell — BF-R023 — Confirmed
The sections below explain what each source actually supports. A promising Bible locator or deed reference is valuable even when the underlying original has not yet been retrieved.

blocks.text: Searches used Beverage, Beveridge, Beveredge, Bevridge and Bevrage with names and places. Beverege and Devrage were added when found in sources. The research queue retains exact logged person queries. Married names, maiden names, initials, neighbors and business associates are included in the continuing queue. A search that finds no usable hit is not evidence that no record exists.

Source states are explicit: original record image, scan of a published edition, edited transcription, institutional narrative, catalog-only entry or inaccessible lead. The 1786 affidavit was read in its 1916 published edition, not as an eighteenth-century manuscript. Cemetery PDFs were read as transcriptions, not stone photographs. Date ranges and question marks are retained.

The early branch needs careful separation of the two James profiles. Published marriage notes and Topsham lists provide useful anchors, but a shared name does not identify the same man across communities. Suspected date errors are review questions, not permission to rewrite the family’s existing account.
Marblehead and Topsham evidence
James Beveredge and Sarah Holman

The Essex Antiquarian reports a February 7, 1733/4 marriage, and Susannah, Mary and Jane living unmarried in Marblehead in 1789 after their mother Sarah’s death. [[SRC119]](https://archive.org/details/essexantiquarian09perluoft)
BF-R004  |  Probable. Published notes cite town records and deeds without a deed locator. Original marriage and 1789 conveyance must be read before adopting the family reconstruction.
Locator: vol. IX (1905), p. 91 Notes. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: james_beveridge_sr_1700
Sarah Holman and Mary White chronology

Sarah Holman’s stored birth date equals her marriage date. Mary White’s stored 1728 birth would make her about two at the recorded 1730 marriage; daughters born after her stored 1731 death also require review. [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1); [[SRC119]](https://archive.org/details/essexantiquarian09perluoft)
BF-R005  |  Conflict. These are incompatible repository fields, not grounds to invent replacement dates. Essex notes assign Susannah, Mary and Jane to Sarah, unlike portions of the repository.
Locator: people.json; events.json; Essex Antiquarian p. 91. Repository comparison: conflicting.
Existing person ID: sarah_holman_1734
James Beverage in Topsham

Wheeler’s town history names James Beverage and William Alexander as hog constables elected at Topsham’s first town meeting, May 9, 1764. [[SRC120]](https://archive.org/details/historyofbrunswi01whee)
BF-R006  |  Probable. The office and name are in the published account; identifying which James requires original town and land records.
Locator: p. 183; citing Topsham town records. Repository comparison: new.
James and Samuel Beveridge Topsham lots
The early land-owner list places James Beveridge at lot 7 in 1758 and Samuel Beveridge at lot 3 in 1752. [[SRC120]](https://archive.org/details/historyofbrunswi01whee)
BF-R007  |  Possible lead. A compiled list is not a deed. Do not infer a sibling relationship or choose between the two James profiles.
Locator: Appendix I p. 869. Repository comparison: new.

dossier.title: Captain Thomas and the Fox Islands

blocks.text: Thomas Beverage
A published sworn statement places Thomas Beverage at Fox Island on June 1, 1786, testifying about a fishing pass he saw in 1781. [[SRC118]](https://sites.rootsweb.com/~mealhn/books/mehist_v21.pdf)

BF-R001  |  Probable. The statement is directly documented; attribution to the repository captain is probable from name, island and chronology. It does not establish Tea Party participation or military service.
Locator: pp. 221–222; PDF 241–242. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: thomas_beverage_1750
Schooner Ann and Thomas Beverage associates

Thomas’s testimony names Robert Duglass, Capt. Henry Mowit, Billings Putnam, Paul Reed and justice William Vinal, and describes a roughly 30-ton schooner Ann. [[SRC118]](https://sites.rootsweb.com/~mealhn/books/mehist_v21.pdf)
BF-R002  |  Confirmed. Confirmed as contents of the published deposition. Duglass’s reported purchase terms are hearsay within Thomas’s testimony; Thomas is not identified as owner.
Locator: pp. 221–222. Repository comparison: new.
Thomas Beverage and Mercy Kent
The Trinity Church published register records Thomas Beverege marrying Mercy Kent on April 13, 1774. [[SRC117]](https://www.colonialsociety.org/node/1104)
BF-R003  |  Confirmed. Published scholarly transcription, not original-register image. Beverege is an attested search variation.
Locator: 1774 April 13 entry. Repository comparison: corroborating.
Existing person ID: thomas_beverage_1750
Thomas Beverage deed chronology

A Woodruff biography cites a Thomas Beverage to James Beverage and others deed under June 28, 1837, after Thomas’s repository death in 1834. [[SRC123]](https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/josiah-beverage); [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)
BF-R011  |  Conflict. Could be recording date, estate action or another Thomas. Original execution and acknowledgment clauses must be checked; no death-date correction is justified.
Locator: DGS 8296915, p. 387, image 207/601. Repository comparison: conflicting.
Existing person ID: thomas_beverage_1750

dossier.title: Diana Daggett and the Kent connections

blocks.text: Diana Daggett baptism

The Doggett-Daggett genealogy identifies Diana’s December 31, 1780 event at Edgartown as baptism, while the repository stores it as birth. [[SRC121]](https://archive.org/details/historyofdoggett00indogg); [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)
BF-R008  |  Conflict. Baptism and birth are different events. Original church entry is required; preserve the repository value pending review.
Locator: Doggett p. 113 entry 1033; people.json. Repository comparison: conflicting.
Existing person ID: diana_daggett_1780
Diana Daggett family cluster

The genealogy gives Diana parents Benjamin Daggett and Elizabeth Hathaway, husband Nathaniel Beverage, and one son and three daughters. [[SRC121]](https://archive.org/details/historyofdoggett00indogg)
BF-R009  |  Probable. Matching husband and date support identity, but this is a compiled genealogy. Its parents’ 1766 intention and church records are still unverified.
Locator: p. 113 entries 809 and 1033. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: diana_daggett_1780
Josiah Beverage and Wilford Woodruff

Woodruff’s April 3, 1838 diary transcription records an afternoon visit to Josiah Devrage; project editors identify him as Josiah Beverage. [[SRC124]](https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/documents/a01dfccc-8bdc-4217-b698-9c1decc9720c/page/3fbc5648-62e1-4222-b482-e1b1b0aa8991); [[SRC123]](https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/josiah-beverage)
BF-R010  |  Strongly supported. Diary text and editorial identity agree with island chronology. A visit does not establish religious conversion or membership.
Locator: Journal p. 25, April 3; subject biography. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: josiah_winslow_beverage_1793
Sarah Beverage Kent and Sarah Sally Beverage

The Kent cemetery transcription calls Sarah Beverage Kent, deceased November 23, 1821 aged 63 years 5 months, a sister of Capt. Thomas. She must not be merged with his daughter Sarah Sally, born 1785. [[SRC092]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/kent_cemetery.pdf); [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)
BF-R012  |  Conflict. Repository links both women to Benjamin Kent 1755. A duplicated transcription line says s.o., the fuller line says sis.o.; use original stone and marriages to distinguish them.
Locator: Kent p. 1, two Sarah entries; two baseline spouse links. Repository comparison: conflicting.
Existing person ID: sarah_beveridge_kent_1758
Benjamin Kent junior and John Kent

Edited Woodruff biographies identify Benjamin Kent (1798–1882) and John Kent (1786–1874) as sons of Benjamin and Sarah Beverage, with spouses Deborah Thomas and Nancy Luce respectively. [[SRC125]](https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/benjamin-kent); [[SRC126]](https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/john-kent)
BF-R013  |  Possible lead. Potential collateral relatives. Do not attach to Sarah born 1785, who could not be John’s mother. Verify town records and the 1793 father’s deed.
Locator: Subject biographies and footnotes. Repository comparison: new.
Benjamin Kent birth month

The edited Benjamin Kent biography gives June 17, 1798 in its narrative and January 17 in a note; Fuller transcription gives June 17. [[SRC125]](https://wilfordwoodruffpapers.org/subjects/benjamin-kent); [[SRC090]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/fuller_cemetery.pdf)
BF-R014  |  Conflict. Internal editorial inconsistency remains unresolved until the cited original vital-record image is checked.
Locator: Benjamin subject notes; Fuller p. 5. Repository comparison: conflicting.

dossier.title: Albert and Olive and the Pulpit Harbor families

blocks.text: Frank Beverage death and spouse

Seaview transcription gives Frank’s death as May 16, 1958 and identifies wife May U. Calderwood. [[SRC091]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/seaview_cemetery.pdf)
BF-R015  |  Probable. Exact January 14, 1861 birth matches baseline, but stone photograph or death certificate has not been obtained.
Locator: p. 2 Frank entry; p. 3 May entry. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: frank_beverage_1861
Frank Beverage farm

NHHS describes a house on Old Barn Hill built in 1819 and a farm inherited by Frank in 1880. [[SRC113]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf)
BF-R016  |  Possible lead. Institutional narrative provides no deed or probate locator. Inheritance source and precise parcel identity require proof; no complete title chain exists here.
Locator: p. 7. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: frank_beverage_1861
Frank Beverage wool trade

NHHS preserves Frank’s recollection of buying island wool for the Knox Woolen Mill in Camden and supplies a photograph of him with an ox dated about 1900. [[SRC111]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/island-grown.html)
BF-R017  |  Confirmed. Confirmed as NHHS attribution and recollection; trade quantities and dates have not been independently audited.
Locator: Frank Beverage recollection and photograph caption. Repository comparison: corroborating.
Existing person ID: frank_beverage_1861
Hiram Beverage farm equipment and images

The museum guide identifies Hiram on a hay rake in a 1917 photograph and describes poultry crates made in winter 1933–1934. [[SRC110]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/farmbuildingguide2019.pdf)
BF-R018  |  Confirmed. Institutional object/photo attribution. Request accession identifiers and permission before website use.
Locator: pp. 13 and 17. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: hiram_stone_beverage_1886
Hiram Beverage egg shipping

The NHHS guide describes Hiram shipping eggs to Boston by steamship in thirty-dozen crates. [[SRC110]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/farmbuildingguide2019.pdf)
BF-R019  |  Confirmed. Confirmed institutional interpretation; no business ledger inspected.
Locator: p. 8. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: hiram_stone_beverage_1886
Hanford W Beverage store

A museum barrel marked H W Beverage is attributed to Hanford W., a Pulpit Harbor storekeeper from 1872 to 1901. [[SRC110]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/farmbuildingguide2019.pdf)
BF-R020  |  Confirmed. Museum attribution is documented. Hanford is a separate research candidate; parentage not established.
Locator: p. 4. Repository comparison: new.
Elmira Carver Beverage and Isa Beverage

NHHS identifies Elmira as Isa’s mother and associates them with the store at the end of Beach Bridge. [[SRC113]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf); [[SRC090]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/fuller_cemetery.pdf)
BF-R021  |  Probable. Institutional account and cemetery family entries agree; deeds and business directory entries remain necessary.
Locator: Village p. 14; Fuller pp. 1–2. Repository comparison: new.
Blue Point and Sky Farm

NHHS describes Alvin and Marion Beverage’s Blue Point farm passing to Nortons then Chestons, and John H. and Cora Beverage’s farm becoming the Lamont estate Sky Farm. [[SRC113]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf)
BF-R022  |  Possible lead. Historical narrative only; transfer dates, legal descriptions and grantees are not proved. No current ownership is asserted.
Locator: p. 7. Repository comparison: new.
Alvin Beverage and church bell

NHHS records Alvin’s bell gift in memory of Orinda, inscribed October 1896 and installed in November after arrival aboard the steamer Tremont. [[SRC114]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_church.pdf)
BF-R023  |  Confirmed. Documented institutional account and copied inscription; Alvin’s exact family placement remains open.
Locator: p. 1. Repository comparison: new.
Beverage Sunday School photograph

A circa 1912 NHHS photograph caption identifies Jennie Beverage, Nettie Crockett, Etta Beverage and Olive Gregory among Mrs. Watts’s class. [[SRC114]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_church.pdf)
BF-R024  |  Confirmed. Caption attribution only. Later married surnames may be retrospective and must not date the marriages.
Locator: p. 9 top photograph. Repository comparison: new.
Nettie Beverage and Malcolm Crockett marriage

The April 20, 1940 Calderwood entry says Malcolm Crockett and Nettie Beverage married the previous evening, indicating April 19. [[SRC106]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1940.pdf); [[SRC090]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/fuller_cemetery.pdf)
BF-R025  |  Strongly supported. Contemporary diary transcription and cemetery spouse attribution agree. Exact date is derived from last evening; certificate not viewed.
Locator: Diary p. 11 April 20; Fuller p. 2 Nettie entry. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: nett_ie_ellen_beverage_1894
Fremont Beverage school superintendent
NHHS cites Fremont’s 1901 superintendent report in its account of the island high school. [[SRC115]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/a-free-high-school.html)
BF-R026  |  Confirmed. Institutional account identifies the office; original town report remains a retrieval target.
Locator: A Free High School, 1901 report paragraph. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: fremont_beverage_1856
Beverage school graduates

NHHS names Elsie, Jennie and Linda Beverage among the first 1907 high school graduates and Nettie Beverage Crockett as class of 1912. [[SRC115]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/a-free-high-school.html)
BF-R027  |  Probable. Documented institutional names; similarly named family members must be identified through school registers before profile attachment.
Locator: Graduation paragraphs. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: nett_ie_ellen_beverage_1894

dossier.title: Eliot and Arnold and the island properties

blocks.text: Eliot Beveridge and IsleBuilt

NHHS identifies Eliot Beveridge as the founder of IsleBuilt in 1955, making boats on North Haven circa 1955–1957 with Penobscot Boat Works in Rockport. [[SRC116]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/islebuilt-boats.html); [[SRC108]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1958.pdf)
BF-R028  |  Strongly supported. Birth/death years and island setting match repository Elliot; diary corroborates local Eliot and Dorothy. Spelling and birth location still require vital records.
Locator: IsleBuilt webpage; diary p. 2. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: elliot_beverage_1908
IsleBuilt models and labor

NHHS lists Sport-O-Ramic, Skim-Skiff and Skim-Fisher models, more than 350 boats and more than ten winter workers; production used the Hopkins Store grain shed. [[SRC116]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/islebuilt-boats.html)
BF-R029  |  Confirmed. Confirmed as museum interpretation. Model dimensions, totals and dates have not been checked against factory accounts.
Locator: Production, models and worker captions. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: elliot_beverage_1908
Eliot and Dorothy return to North Haven

NHHS says Eliot and wife Dorothy returned permanently in 1954; January 1958 diary entries name both in island social and work activities. [[SRC116]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/islebuilt-boats.html); [[SRC108]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1958.pdf)
BF-R030  |  Strongly supported. Two sources support residence and partnership; Dorothy’s maiden name and marriage certificate remain unverified.
Locator: IsleBuilt biography; diary p. 2 January 11–21. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: elliot_beverage_1908
Beveridge Point wood hauling

The Calderwood diary records hauling about five cords from Beveridge’s Point for Eliot Beveridge on January 21, 1958, assisted by Berger Yonquist. [[SRC108]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1958.pdf)
BF-R031  |  Confirmed. Direct diary transcription evidence of activity and place name; does not establish legal ownership or a modern parcel boundary.
Locator: p. 2 January 21 entry. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: elliot_beverage_1908
Eliot birthplace and name

The repository calls him Elliot Pierson Beverage born North Haven; NHHS calls him Eliot Beveridge born Massachusetts in 1908. [[SRC116]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/islebuilt-boats.html); [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)
BF-R032  |  Conflict. Years and island career suggest the same person, but original birth and Harvard records are needed. Preserve both spellings and locations.
Locator: IsleBuilt biography; elliot_beverage_1908. Repository comparison: conflicting.
Existing person ID: elliot_beverage_1908
Arnold P Beveridge island registrations
Maine’s registry names Arnold P. Beveridge for Sheep Island 63-018, with deed book 495 page 361, and Little Island 63-019, book 164 page 370. [[SRC122]](https://www.maine.gov/dacf/parks/docs/CIR.pdf)

BF-R033  |  Confirmed. Confirmed registry entries; proposed identity matches full name and locality but needs the deeds. Registration dates are not deed dates. Registry is not a current ownership record.
Locator: p. 27, 63-018 and 63-019. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: arnold_beveridge_1903

dossier.title: Orris and Lowell and the education branches

blocks.text: Lowell Beverage piano performance
A Calderwood entry records Lowell Beverage playing piano at church on August 9, 1925. [[SRC104]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1925.pdf)
BF-R034  |  Probable. First name, island and musical career fit; middle name absent. Do not attribute to another Lowell or assume a formal appointment.
Locator: p. 12 August 9. Repository comparison: new.

Lowell Beveridge portrait

Columbia catalog item 7250 identifies a Lowell Pierson Beveridge portrait in University Archives Historical Photographs Box 9. [[SRC127]](https://exhibitions.library.columbia.edu/exhibits/show/music-centennial/item/7250)
BF-R035  |  Confirmed. Catalog identification confirmed; date retains catalog question mark. High-resolution file and reuse rights not confirmed.
Locator: Item 7250; Historical Photographs Box 9. Repository comparison: new.

Lowell chapel appointment

Columbia’s chapel history gives Lowell’s organist and director of chapel music tenure as 1937–1952, distinct from his broader 1930–1952 faculty service. [[SRC128]](https://exhibitions.library.columbia.edu/exhibits/show/music-centennial/music-performance--the-early-y/st--paul-s-chapel)
BF-R036  |  Confirmed. Avoid treating different job titles as a contradiction. Earlier newspaper appointments still require checking.
Locator: St Pauls Chapel section. Repository comparison: corroborating.

Lowell manuscript Universal Harmony

The diocesan memorial reports a roughly 2,000-page manuscript titled Universal Harmony held at the seminary. [[SRC129]](https://episcopalvirginia.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1991-Diocese_Journal_searchable.pdf)

BF-R037  |  Possible lead. Historical location reported in 1991; present custody, extent and access have not been confirmed. Baseline obituary may already mention this; useful retrieval specification, not claimed wholly new biography.
Locator: p. 73; PDF p. 38. Repository comparison: new.
Existing person ID: lowell_beveridge_1905
Lyford Beveridge missing sibling

Lowell’s diocesan memorial identifies a surviving brother Lyford Beveridge of Rockland; that brother is absent from the repository’s Orris children list. [[SRC129]](https://episcopalvirginia.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1991-Diocese_Journal_searchable.pdf); [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)

BF-R038  |  Possible lead. Do not create a parent-child link from a single obituary-derived statement. May duplicate the existing Washington Post source; independent birth or census evidence is needed.
Locator: p. 73; Orris child list. Repository comparison: new.
Lowell memorial age and birthplace

The diocesan memorial prints 1905-09-19 to 1991-06-18 but calls Lowell 86; those dates yield 85. It calls him a Boston native, while the repository retains North Haven birthplace. [[SRC129]](https://episcopalvirginia.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1991-Diocese_Journal_searchable.pdf); [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)

blocks.text: These are research starting points rather than legal title findings. [[SRC122]](https://www.maine.gov/dacf/parks/docs/CIR.pdf); [[SRC108]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/1958.pdf); [[SRC113]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/pulpit_harbor_village.pdf); [[SRC120]](https://archive.org/details/historyofbrunswi01whee)

The sources connect island life to wider markets and institutions: Hiram’s eggs went to Boston, Frank recalled wool trading with Camden, and IsleBuilt worked with Rockport. Lowell’s institutional career takes the research to New York and Virginia, while Diana’s genealogy points to Martha’s Vineyard and Dartmouth. These connections guide searches; they do not prove residence at every place mentioned. [[SRC110]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/uploads/5/2/8/7/5287313/farmbuildingguide2019.pdf); [[SRC111]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/island-grown.html); [[SRC116]](https://www.northhavenmainehistoricalsociety.org/islebuilt-boats.html); [[SRC128]](https://exhibitions.library.columbia.edu/exhibits/show/music-centennial/music-performance--the-early-y/st--paul-s-chapel); [[SRC129]](https://episcopalvirginia.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/1991-Diocese_Journal_searchable.pdf); [[SRC121]](https://archive.org/details/historyofdoggett00indogg)

The baseline already warns that North Haven’s earlier records may appear under Vinalhaven and older county jurisdictions. Search by the event’s date and jurisdiction. A modern municipal map point or cemetery coordinate is not the location of a historical house, wireless station or deed boundary. [[SRC001]](https://github.com/csully1234/Beverage-Family/tree/4e3d4860d3c8d9ae9cbcb19567dafa17e1a93db1)

The Boston Tea Party participation statement is preserved. The 1786 affidavit provides a new historical context for a Thomas Beverage but neither establishes nor disproves his presence at the Tea Party. No conclusion about recognition by a museum or commemorative body is made without its underlying record.

Existing relative addresses and family-property fields are retained only as baseline entries. Research did not promote newly encountered private current addresses, phone numbers, financial information or private-account details. Institutional archive contacts are included to support retrieval.

All eleven curated conflicts are collected in the workbook. Some are new comparisons; others, such as Lowell’s birthplace, were already noted by the repository and are carried forward. The automated baseline audit additionally reports one-sided relationships, unresolved targets and January 1 precision candidates. Those audit flags are not automatically eleven-plus-new historical contradictions.
1. Family Bible pages — BF-G001. What do the earliest surviving family entries actually say about Thomas, Mercy, Albert and Olive?
2. Arnold island deeds — BF-G002. Which conveyances underlie the two historical registrations?
3. Thomas deed cited in 1837 — BF-G003. Was the 1837 date execution, recording, an estate transaction or another Thomas?
4. Marblehead marriages and 1789 deed — BF-G004. Which James married each woman, and who were the mothers of Susannah, Mary and Jane?
5. North Haven vital records and stones — BF-G005. Which conflicting exact dates are correct?
6. Sarah Kent identity — BF-G006. Which Sarah married Benjamin Kent, and which children belong to that couple?
7. Diana Daggett baptism and parents — BF-G007. Is December 31, 1780 baptism rather than birth, and are the stated parents correct?
8. Eliot biography and Harvard records — BF-G008. Was Eliot born in Massachusetts, who was Dorothy, and which degrees did he receive?
9. IsleBuilt archive and surviving boat — BF-G009. What company records, plans, advertisements and photographs survive?
10. 1850 James and Lucy notice — BF-G010. What exactly does the contemporary death notice report, and does any source support the poisoning tradition?
The separate Research Gaps document includes all 33 retrieval packets, practical routes, request language, known fees and uncertainties. Nothing was sent to any archive or person.

Keep SRC identifiers stable when adding a new access URL to an existing work. Create a new BF-R identifier for a genuinely new finding, not for each sheet where it appears. When an original is obtained, record what was viewed, exact locator and the reasoning for any confidence change. Preserve superseded hypotheses in the conflict history. Website candidates remain unreviewed until a family reviewer accepts the wording and supporting record.

Bracketed SRC numbers link the narrative to this bibliography and the full Source Register. Access date for this research volume is 2026-10-14. The complete register also includes baseline citations that were inventoried without reopening their underlying records.
